title.en: Volume 27 Biographies 19: He Lianda; Han Guo; Cai You; Chang Shan; Xin Wei; She Dichang; Tian Hong; Liang Chun; Liang Tai; Yu Wence brother Shen
title.raw: 卷27 列傳第19 赫連達 韓果 蔡祐 常善 辛威 厙狄昌 田弘 梁椿 梁臺 宇文測 弟深 Volume 27 Biographies 19: He Lianda; Han Guo; Cai You; Chang Shan; Xin Wei; She Dichang; Tian Hong; Liang Chun; Liang Tai; Yu Wence brother Shen

sentences.zh: 赫連達 韓果 蔡祐 常善 辛威 厙狄昌 田弘 梁椿 梁臺 宇文測 弟深

translations.literal: He Lianda; Han Guo; Cai You; Chang Shan; Xin Wei; Shedichang; Tian Hong; Liang Chun; Liang Tai; Yuwen Ce; younger brother Shen
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda; Han Guo; Cai You; Chang Shan; Xin Wei; Shedichang; Tian Hong; Liang Chun; Liang Tai; Yuwen Ce; Yuwen Shen (younger brother)

sentences.zh: 赫連達字朔周，盛樂人，勃勃之後也。

translations.literal: He Lianda, styled Shuozhou, was a man of Shengle, a descendant of Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda, styled Shuozhou, came from Shengle and traced his descent to Bobo.

sentences.zh: 曾祖庫多汗，因避難改姓杜氏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuduohan, to escape disaster, changed his surname to the Du clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuduohan had taken the surname Du while fleeing trouble.

sentences.zh: 達性剛鯁，有膽力。

translations.literal: Da by nature was stiffly upright and had daring strength.
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda was blunt and resolute by nature, fearless and strong.

sentences.zh: 少從賀拔岳征討有功，拜都將，賜爵長廣鄉男，遷都督。

translations.literal: From youth he followed He Ba Yue on campaigns and suppressions with merit; appointed Division Commander, granted noble rank as Baron of Changguang Township, promoted to Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he campaigned under He Ba Yue with distinction, was made division commander and Baron of Changguang Township, then area commander.

sentences.zh: 及岳為侯莫陳悅所害，軍中大擾。

translations.literal: When Yue was murdered by Houmochen Yue, the army fell into great turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Houmochen Yue murdered He Ba Yue, the army was thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 趙貴建議迎太祖，諸將猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui proposed welcoming the Grand Progenitor, but the various generals hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui urged them to welcome Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, but the other generals wavered and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「宇文夏州昔為左丞，明略過人，一時之傑。

translations.literal: Da said: "Yuwen of Xia Province formerly served as Left Assistant, his wisdom and strategy surpassing men—a hero of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda said: "Yuwen Tai of Xia Province once served as left assistant; his insight surpasses other men—he is the hero of our time.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，非此公不濟。

translations.literal: Today's affair cannot succeed without this lord.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing we face today can succeed without him.

sentences.zh: 趙將軍議是也。

translations.literal: General Zhao's proposal is correct.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhao is right.

sentences.zh: 達請輕騎告哀，仍迎之。

translations.literal: Da requests light cavalry to report the mourning and at once welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Let me take a light detachment to announce what has happened and bring him back.

sentences.zh: 」諸將或欲南追賀拔勝，或云東告朝廷。

translations.literal: " Some generals wished to pursue He Ba Sheng southward, or said they should report east to the court.
translations.idiomatic: " Some generals wanted to ride south after He Ba Sheng; others said they should send word east to the court.

sentences.zh: 達又曰：「此皆遠水不救近火，何足道哉。

translations.literal: Da again said: "These are all distant water that cannot save a nearby fire—what is there to speak of?"
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda said again: "That is distant water for a nearby fire—worthless."

sentences.zh: 」貴於是謀遂定，令達馳往。

translations.literal: Gui thereupon fixed the plan, and ordered Da to gallop there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui then settled the plan and sent He Lianda riding ahead.

sentences.zh: 太祖見達慟哭，問故，達以實對。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, seeing Da, wept bitterly and asked the reason; Da answered with the facts.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai saw He Lianda he wept and asked what had happened; He Lianda told him the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 太祖遂以數百騎南赴平涼，引軍向高平，令達率騎據彈箏峽。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon with several hundred horsemen went south to Pingliang, led the army toward Gaoping, and ordered Da to lead cavalry to hold Tancheng Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then rode south to Pingliang with a few hundred men, marched the army toward Gaoping, and put He Lianda in charge of cavalry holding Tancheng Gorge.

sentences.zh: 時百姓惶懼，奔散者多。

translations.literal: At the time the common people were fearful and alarmed, and many fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The people were terrified, and many had already fled.

sentences.zh: 有數村民，方扶老弱、驅畜牧，欲入山避難，軍士爭欲掠之。

translations.literal: Several village folk were just supporting the old and weak and driving livestock and herds, wishing to enter the mountains to escape disaster, when soldiers competed to plunder them.
translations.idiomatic: A few villagers were shepherding the elderly and weak and their herds toward the hills when soldiers began fighting over the chance to loot them.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「遠近民黎，多受制於賊，今若值便掠縛，何謂伐罪弔民！

translations.literal: Da said: "Near and far, the people are mostly subject to the bandits; if we seize the chance to bind and plunder them, what would it mean to punish crime and comfort the people!
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda said: "People near and far are already at the rebels' mercy. If we seize and plunder them now, how can we call ourselves an army punishing wrongdoers and succoring the people?

sentences.zh: 不如因而撫之，以示義師之德。

translations.literal: Better to take the occasion to soothe them, to show the righteous army's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: We should soothe them instead and show what a righteous army stands for.

sentences.zh: 」乃撫以恩信，民皆悅附，於是迭相曉語，咸復舊業。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he soothed them with kindness and trust, and the people all gladly attached themselves; thus they told one another in turn, and all resumed their old occupations.
translations.idiomatic: " He won them over with kindness and good faith, and the people gladly rallied to him; word spread from village to village, and they returned to their old livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, hearing of it, commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai heard of it and praised him.

sentences.zh: 悅平，加平東將軍。

translations.literal: When Yue was pacified, [Da] was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue was defeated, He Lianda was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂諸將曰：「當清水公遇禍之時，君等性命懸於賊手，雖欲來告，其路無從。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said to the various generals: "When Duke of Qingshui met calamity, your lives hung in the bandits' hands; though you wished to come report, there was no road.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai told the generals: "When the Duke of Qingshui was killed, your lives were in the rebels' hands. Even if you had wanted to reach me, there was no way.

sentences.zh: 杜朔周冒萬死之難，遠來見及，遂得共盡忠節，同雪讐恥。

translations.literal: Du Shuozhou braved the danger of ten thousand deaths, came from afar and reached me, and thus we were able together to exhaust loyalty and integrity and jointly wipe away vengeance and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shuozhou risked death to ride to me from afar, and only then could we all serve with full loyalty and wipe away our shame together.

sentences.zh: 雖藉衆人之力，實賴杜子之功。

translations.literal: Though relying on the strength of the multitude, in truth it depended on Master Du's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: We had the strength of many men, but in truth we owed the victory to Du.

sentences.zh: 勞而不酬，何以勸善。

translations.literal: Labor without reward—how can one encourage good?"
translations.idiomatic: Reward such labor, or how will anyone be moved to do good?"

sentences.zh: 」乃賜馬二百匹。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 達固讓，太祖弗許。

translations.literal: Da firmly declined, but the Grand Progenitor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda refused repeatedly, but Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武入關，褒敘勳義，以達首逆元帥，匡復秦、隴，進爵魏昌縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei entered the Pass, commending achievements and righteousness; because Da was first to oppose the commander-in-chief and restore Qin and Long, he was advanced in noble rank to Earl of Weichang County, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei entered the Pass and rewarded loyal service, He Lianda was raised to Earl of Weichang County with a fief of five hundred households for being first to rally to the commander-in-chief and recover Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 從儀同李虎破曹泥，除鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫，加通直散騎常侍，增邑幷前一千戶。

translations.literal: Following Colonel-in-Ordinary Li Hu in breaking Cao Ni, removed [from current post] and made General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, added Directly Attached Regular Attendant Cavalier, fief increased together with previous to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After serving under Colonel-in-Ordinary Li Hu in the defeat of Cao Ni, he was made General Who Guards the South and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the added title Directly Attached Regular Attendant Cavalier and a combined fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 從復弘農，戰沙苑，皆有功。

translations.literal: Following the recovery of Hongnong, fighting at Shaye—all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought in the recovery of Hongnong and at Shaye, earning merit in both.

sentences.zh: 又增邑八百戶，除

translations.literal: Fief again increased by eight hundred households; removed [from current post] and made Administrator of
translations.idiomatic: His fief was increased by eight hundred households, and he was appointed administrator of

translations.literal: (Quan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Quan]

sentences.zh: 〔白水〕郡守，轉帥都督，加持節，除濟州刺史。

translations.literal: [Bai Shui] commandery, transferred to Area Commander-in-Chief, granted staff of authority, removed [from current post] and made Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Shui commandery, promoted to area commander-in-chief with staff of authority, and then governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 詔復姓赫連氏。

translations.literal: An edict restored the surname Helian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the Helian surname.

sentences.zh: 以達勳望兼隆，乃除雲州刺史，卽本州也。

translations.literal: Because Da's achievements and reputation were both lofty, he was then removed [from current post] and made Governor of Yun Province—it was his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Because He Lianda's record and standing were both high, he was made governor of Yun Province, his home province.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公，拜大都督，尋授儀同三司。

translations.literal: Advanced in noble rank to Duke, appointed Grand Area Commander, and soon granted Colonel-in-Ordinary of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to duke and grand area commander, and soon received the rank of colonel-in-ordinary of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 從大將軍達奚武攻漢中。

translations.literal: Following Grand General Daxi Wu in attacking Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand General Daxi Wu in the attack on Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 梁宜豐侯蕭循拒守積時，後乃送款。

translations.literal: Liang's Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun resisted and defended for a long time, and afterward sent overtures of submission.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xun, Marquis of Yifeng of Liang, held out for a long time before at last offering to surrender.

sentences.zh: 武問諸將進止之宜。

translations.literal: Wu asked the various generals the proper course of advance or halt.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu asked his generals whether to press the attack or hold back.

sentences.zh: 開府賀蘭願德等以其食盡，欲急攻取之。

translations.literal: Bureau Chief Helan Yuande and others, because their provisions were exhausted, wished to attack and take it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Chief Helan Yuande and others, seeing the enemy's stores spent, wanted a swift assault.

sentences.zh: 達曰：「不戰而獲城，策之上者。

translations.literal: Da said: "Taking a city without fighting is the highest stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda said: "To take a city without fighting is the best strategy.

sentences.zh: 無容利其子女，貪其財帛。

translations.literal: One must not tolerate profiting from their women and children or coveting their wealth and silks.
translations.idiomatic: We must not prey on their families or covet their goods.

sentences.zh: 窮兵極武，仁者不為。

translations.literal: Exhausting the army to the utmost in warfare—the humane do not do this.
translations.idiomatic: To grind the army down in total war is not what a humane commander does.

sentences.zh: 且觀其士馬猶強，城池尚固，攻之縱克，必將彼此俱損。

translations.literal: Moreover, observe that their soldiers and horses are still strong and the walls and moat still firm; even if the attack succeeds and is taken, both sides will surely suffer damage.
translations.idiomatic: Their men and horses are still strong and the walls still hold; even if we took the place, both sides would be badly hurt.

sentences.zh: 如其困獸猶鬥，則成敗未可知。

translations.literal: If they fight like cornered beasts, then success or defeat cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: If they fight like cornered beasts, the outcome is anyone's guess.

sentences.zh: 況行師之道，以全軍為上。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the way of marching armies, preserving the whole army is supreme.
translations.idiomatic: And in war the first duty is to bring the whole army home.

sentences.zh: 」武曰：「公言是也。

translations.literal: " Wu said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: " Daxi Wu said: "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」乃命將帥各申所見。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the commanders each to state their views.
translations.idiomatic: He then had each commander give his opinion.

sentences.zh: 於是開府楊寬等並同達議，武遂受循降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bureau Chief Yang Kuan and others all agreed with Da's proposal, and Wu then accepted Xun's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Chief Yang Kuan and the others sided with He Lianda, and Daxi Wu accepted Xiao Xun's surrender.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，進爵藍田縣公。

translations.literal: When the army returned, [Da] was transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Bureau Chief Colonel-in-Ordinary of the Third Rank, added Palace Attendant, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Lantian County.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, He Lianda was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and bureau chief of the third rank, with palace attendant added, and was raised to Duke of Lantian County.

sentences.zh: 六官初建，授左遂伯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were first established, [he was] granted Left Suibo.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were first established, he was made Left Suibo.

sentences.zh: 出為隴州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent out as Governor of Long Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Long Province.

sentences.zh: 保定初，遷大將軍、夏州總管、三州五防諸軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, transferred to Grand General, Overall Commander of Xia Province, and overall command of military affairs for the Three Provinces and Five Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Baoding he was made grand general and overall commander of Xia Province with authority over the three provinces and five garrisons.

sentences.zh: 達雖非文吏，然性質直，遵奉法度，輕於鞭撻，而重慎死罪。

translations.literal: Though Da was not a literary official, by nature he was straightforward, observed and followed the law, was light with the whip and cudgel yet heavy and cautious with capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda was no clerk, but he was plainspoken, strict about the law, sparing with the lash yet careful and reluctant to impose death.

sentences.zh: 性又廉儉，邊境胡民或饋達以羊者，達欲招納異類，報以繒帛。

translations.literal: By nature he was also frugal and modest; border Hu people sometimes presented Da with sheep; Da, wishing to win over other peoples, repaid them with silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was also frugal. Border tribesmen sometimes gave him sheep; wishing to win them over, he repaid them from his own stores of silk.

sentences.zh: 主司請用官物，達曰：「羊入我廚，物出官庫，是欺上也。

translations.literal: The supervising office requested using official goods; Da said: "Sheep enter my kitchen, goods leave the official storehouse—this is deceiving one's superior."
translations.idiomatic: His staff wanted to use government goods, but He Lianda said: "If sheep enter my kitchen while goods leave the public storehouse, I am cheating my superiors."

sentences.zh: 」命取私帛與之。

translations.literal: He ordered private silks taken to give them.
translations.idiomatic: He had his own silk brought out instead.

sentences.zh: 識者嘉其仁恕焉。

translations.literal: Those who knew commended his benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment praised his kindness and restraint.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵樂川郡公。

translations.literal: Soon advanced in noble rank to Duke of Lechuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to Duke of Lechuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，進位柱國，薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande, advanced in rank to Pillar of State; died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiande he was made Pillar of State, then died.

sentences.zh: 子遷嗣。

translations.literal: His son Qian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大象中位至大將軍、蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era he reached the rank of Grand General and Governor of Pu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era Qian rose to grand general and governor of Pu Province.

sentences.zh: 韓果字阿六拔，代武川人也。

translations.literal: Han Guo, styled A Liubba, was a man of Dai's Wuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guo, styled A Liubba, came from Wuchuan in Dai.

sentences.zh: 少驍雄，善騎射。

translations.literal: From youth he was fierce and heroic, skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was bold and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳西征，引為帳內。

translations.literal: He Ba Yue on the western expedition took him into his tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: On his western campaign He Ba Yue took Han Guo into his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 擊万俟醜奴及其枝黨，轉戰數十合，並破之。

translations.literal: Attacking Wanqidu Chounu and his branch factions, he turned and fought several dozen engagements, and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Wanqidu Chounu and his allies in dozens of battles and broke them every time.

sentences.zh: 膂力絕倫，被甲荷戈，升陟峰嶺，猶涉平路，雖數十百日，不以為勞。

translations.literal: His physical strength was unmatched; clad in armor and bearing halberd, ascending and descending peaks and ridges, he still crossed as on level road—even after several tens or hundreds of days, he did not regard it as toil.
translations.idiomatic: His strength was unmatched: armored and weapon in hand, he climbed peaks as if on flat ground and could march tens or hundreds of days without tiring.

sentences.zh: 以功授宣

translations.literal: For merit granted General of Xuan
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made General of Xuan

translations.literal: (Wu)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Wu]

sentences.zh: 〔威〕將軍、子都督。

translations.literal: [Wei], Sub-area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: General of Xuanwei and sub-area commander.

sentences.zh: 從太祖討平侯莫陳悅，遷都督，賜爵邯鄲縣男。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor in suppressing and pacifying Houmochen Yue, transferred to Area Commander, granted noble rank as Baron of Handan County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in defeating Houmochen Yue, was made area commander, and enfeoffed as Baron of Handan County.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武入關，進爵石〔城〕縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Wei entered the Pass, advanced in noble rank to Earl of Shi [Cheng] County, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei entered the Pass, Han Guo was raised to Earl of Shicheng County with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統初，進爵為公，增邑通前一千戶，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, advanced in noble rank to Duke, fief increased together with previous to one thousand households, added Directly Attached Regular Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he was raised to duke with a combined fief of one thousand households and given the title Directly Attached Regular Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 果性強記，兼有權略。

translations.literal: Guo by nature had a strong memory and also possessed strategic resourcefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Han Guo had a powerful memory and a gift for strategy.

sentences.zh: 所行之處，山川形勢，備能記憶。

translations.literal: Wherever he traveled, the mountains, rivers, and terrain—he could fully remember them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he marched, he memorized every feature of the land.

sentences.zh: 兼善伺敵虛實，揣知情狀，有潛匿溪穀欲為間偵者，果登高望之，所疑處，往必有獲。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at observing the enemy's emptiness and fullness and inferring their circumstances; those who hid in streams and valleys wishing to spy secretly—Guo would ascend high and look out, and wherever he suspected, going there he always had captures.
translations.idiomatic: He could read an enemy's strength and intentions; when scouts hid in ravines, he climbed to a height, marked the place, and always found them.

sentences.zh: 太祖由是以果為虞候都督。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereby made Guo Scout Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai therefore made him scout commander.

sentences.zh: 每從征行，常領候騎，晝夜巡察，略不眠寢。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed on campaign, he always led the scout cavalry, patrolling day and night, scarcely sleeping or resting.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign he led the scout cavalry, riding patrol day and night with almost no sleep.

sentences.zh: 從襲竇泰於潼關，太祖依其規畫，軍以勝返。

translations.literal: Following the surprise attack on Dou Tai at Tong Pass, the Grand Progenitor relied on his planning, and the army returned victorious.
translations.idiomatic: At the surprise attack on Dou Tai at Tong Pass, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai followed his plan and the army returned in victory.

sentences.zh: 賞真珠金帶一腰、帛二百匹，授征虜將軍。

translations.literal: Rewarded with one belt of true pearls and gold, two hundred bolts of silk, and granted General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with a belt of pearls and gold, two hundred bolts of silk, and the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 又從復弘農，攻拔河南城，獲郡守一人，論功為最。

translations.literal: Again following the recovery of Hongnong, attacking and taking Henan city, capturing one commandery administrator—the merit reckoned as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again in the recovery of Hongnong, took Henan city, and captured a commandery administrator; his merit was judged the greatest.

sentences.zh: 破沙苑，戰河橋，並有功，授撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫，增邑九百戶。

translations.literal: Breaking Shaye, fighting at Heqiao—all had merit; granted General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, fief increased nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Shaye and Heqiao with distinction, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon, and received nine hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 遷朔州刺史，轉安州刺史，加帥都督。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Shuo Province, transferred to Governor of An Province, added Area Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Shuo Province, then of An Province, with area commander-in-chief added.

sentences.zh: 九年，從戰邙山，軍還，除河東郡守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, following the battle at Mount Mang, when the army returned, removed [from current post] and made Administrator of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he fought at Mount Mang, and when the army returned he was made administrator of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 又從大軍破稽胡於北山。

translations.literal: Again following the great army in breaking the Ji Hu at North Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the main army again in defeating the Ji Hu at North Mountain.

sentences.zh: 胡地險阻，人迹罕至，果進兵窮討，散其種落。

translations.literal: The Hu lands were perilous and obstructed, human tracks rarely reached; Guo advanced troops in exhaustive pursuit and scattered their clans and bands.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji Hu country was rugged and almost untraveled; Han Guo drove deep in pursuit and broke up their tribes.

sentences.zh: 稽胡憚果勁健，號為著翅人。

translations.literal: The Ji Hu feared Guo's vigor and strength, and called him the Winged Man.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji Hu feared his strength and called him the Winged Man.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，笑曰：「著翅之名，寧減飛將。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, hearing of it, laughed and said: "The name Winged—surely it does not fall short of the Flying General.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai laughed when he heard it and said: "Winged Man is a name that need not bow to the Flying General.

sentences.zh: 」累遷大都督、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，出為宜州刺史。

translations.literal: " Repeatedly promoted to Grand Area Commander, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel-in-Ordinary of the Third Rank, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Bureau Chief Colonel-in-Ordinary of the Third Rank, sent out as Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: " He rose through grand area commander, grand general of chariots and cavalry, colonel-in-ordinary of the third rank, grand general of agile cavalry, and bureau chief of the third rank, and was sent out as governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，進爵褒中郡公。

translations.literal: Recording achievements before and after, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Baozhong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated service won him promotion to Duke of Baozhong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，授大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, granted Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 從賀蘭祥討吐谷渾，以功別封一子縣公。

translations.literal: Following Helan Xiang in suppressing Tuyuhun, for merit separately enfeoffed one son as County Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Helan Xiang against Tuyuhun and, for his merit, had one son separately enfeoffed as county duke.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，又率軍破稽胡，大獲生口。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng, again led troops and broke the Ji Hu, greatly capturing living captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wucheng he led troops again, broke the Ji Hu, and took many captives.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢一百口，除寧州刺史。

translations.literal: Granted one hundred male and female slaves, removed [from current post] and made Governor of Ning Province.
translations.idiomatic: He received one hundred slaves and was made governor of Ning Province.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，拜少師，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, appointed Junior Preceptor, advanced in rank to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding he was made junior preceptor and raised to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 四年，從尉遲迥圍洛陽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, following Yuchi Jiong in besieging Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed Yuchi Jiong in the siege of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 軍退，果所部獨全。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, only Guo's division remained wholly intact.
translations.idiomatic: When the army withdrew, only Han Guo's command came back intact.

sentences.zh: 天和初，授華州刺史，為政寬簡，吏民稱之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe, granted Governor of Hua Province; in governing he was broad and simple, and officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianhe he was made governor of Hua Province; his rule was easy and plain, and officials and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 建德初，薨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande, he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jiande he died.

sentences.zh: 子明嗣。

translations.literal: Ziming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ziming succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至上大將軍、黎州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, he reached the rank of Upper Grand General and Governor of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Daxiang he had risen to upper grand general and governor of Li Province.

sentences.zh: 與尉遲迥同謀，被誅。

translations.literal: He joined Yuchi Jiong in a plot and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yuchi Jiong in a conspiracy and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 蔡祐字承先，其先陳留圉人也。

translations.literal: Cai You, styled Chengxian, his forebears were men of Yu in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You, styled Chengxian, came from Yu in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖紹為夏州鎮將，徙居高平，因家焉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shao served as garrison commander of Xia Province, moved to dwell at Gaoping, and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shao had been garrison commander of Xia Province, moved to Gaoping, and settled the family there.

sentences.zh: 祖護，魏景明初，為陳留郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hu, at the beginning of Jingming in Wei, served as Administrator of Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hu served as administrator of Chenliu commandery at the start of the Wei Jingming era.

sentences.zh: 父襲，名著西州。

translations.literal: His father Xi was famed throughout Western Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi was renowned throughout the west.

sentences.zh: 正光中，万俟醜奴寇亂關中，襲乃背賊，棄妻子，歸洛陽。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era, Wan Qidu Chounu raided and ravaged Guanzhong; Xi then turned against the bandits, abandoned wife and children, and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguang, Wan Qidu Chounu ravaged Guanzhong; Xi then broke with the rebels, left his wife and children behind, and fled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 拜齊安郡守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Qi'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Qi'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武西遷，仍在關東。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he remained in the eastern lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Xi remained in the east.

sentences.zh: 後始拔難西歸，賜爵平舒縣伯，除岐、夏二州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Only afterward did he break free and return west, was granted noble rank as Baron of Pingshu County, removed [from current post] and made Governor of Qi and Xia provinces, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he escape and return west; he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingshu County, made governor of Qi and Xia provinces, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈原州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 祐性聰敏，有行檢。

translations.literal: You by nature was clever and keen, with moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You was clever and principled by nature.

sentences.zh: 襲之背賊東歸也，祐年十四，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: When Xi turned against the bandits and returned east, You was fourteen and served his mother with filial piety that won renown.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi broke with the rebels and returned east, You was fourteen and won fame for serving his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及長，有膂力，便騎射。

translations.literal: When grown, he had physical strength and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was powerfully built and skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 太祖在原州，召為帳下親信。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was at Yuan Province and summoned him as a trusted attendant in his personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was at Yuan Province he summoned Cai You into his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖遷夏州，以祐為都督。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor moved to Xia Province, he made You area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai moved to Xia Province he made Cai You area commander.

sentences.zh: 及侯莫陳悅害賀拔岳，諸將遣使迎太祖。

translations.literal: When Houmochen Yue murdered He Ba Yue, the various generals sent envoys to welcome the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue murdered He Ba Yue, the generals sent envoys to welcome Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 將赴，夏州首望彌姐元進等陰有異計。

translations.literal: About to go, the leading clan heads of Xia Province, Mizhi Yuanjin and others, secretly harbored a different plan.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to go, the leading clan heads of Xia Province, Mizhi Yuanjin and others, secretly plotted treachery.

sentences.zh: 太祖微知之，先與祐議執元進。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor faintly knew it and first discussed with You seizing Yuanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had a hint of it and first discussed with Cai You seizing Yuanjin.

sentences.zh: 祐曰：「狼子野心，會當反噬，今若執縛，不如殺之。

translations.literal: You said: "A wolf cub has the heart of a wolf; in time it will turn and bite. If we bind him now, better to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You said: "A wolf cub has a wolf's heart; in time it will turn and bite. If we seize him now, we had better kill him.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「汝大決也。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said: "You are very decisive.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "You are very decisive.

sentences.zh: 」於是召元進等入計事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he summoned Yuanjin and the others to enter and discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He then summoned Yuanjin and the others in to discuss plans.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「隴賊逆亂，與諸人戮力討之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor said: "The Long bandits rebel and run riot; let us join forces to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "The Long rebels are in revolt; let us join forces to punish them.

sentences.zh: 觀諸人輩似有不同者。

translations.literal: Looking at you all, some seem to have different views.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some of you seem to have other ideas.

sentences.zh: 」太祖微以此言動之，因目祐。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor faintly used these words to stir them, and thereupon signaled You with his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: " He used these words to probe them, then signaled Cai You with his eyes.

sentences.zh: 祐卽出外，衣甲持刀直入，瞋目叱諸人曰：「與人朝謀夕異，豈是人也！

translations.literal: You immediately went outside, donned armor, took a blade, and entered straight in; glaring, he shouted at the assembly: "To plot with a man in the morning and turn different in the evening—is that the conduct of a human being!
translations.idiomatic: Cai You at once went out, put on armor, took a sword, and strode back in. Glaring at the assembly he shouted: "To plot with a man in the morning and turn against him by evening—is that how a man behaves?

sentences.zh: 蔡祐今日必斬姦人之頭。

translations.literal: Cai You today will surely cut off the traitors' heads.
translations.idiomatic: Today Cai You will cut off the traitors' heads.

sentences.zh: 」因按劍臨之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon pressed his sword upon them.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed his hand to his sword and advanced on them.

sentences.zh: 舉座皆叩頭曰：「願有簡擇。

translations.literal: The whole assembly all kowtowed and said: "We wish there to be selection.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly kowtowed and said: "Choose among us as you will.

sentences.zh: 」祐乃叱元進而斬之，幷其黨並伏誅。

translations.literal: " You then shouted down Yuanjin and beheaded him, and together with his faction all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: " Cai You then denounced Yuanjin and beheaded him, and his whole faction was put to death.

sentences.zh: 一坐皆戰慄，不敢仰視。

translations.literal: The whole assembly trembled with fear and dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: The whole assembly trembled and dared not raise their eyes.

sentences.zh: 於是與諸將結盟，同心誅悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he joined the various generals in alliance, of one mind to execute Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the generals in alliance, resolved together to kill Houmochen Yue.

sentences.zh: 太祖以此知重之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereby came to know and value him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai thereby came to know and value him.

sentences.zh: 乃謂祐曰：「吾今以爾為子，爾其父事我。

translations.literal: He then said to You: "I now take you as my son; you should serve me as a father.
translations.idiomatic: He then told Cai You: "I now take you as my son; serve me as you would a father.

sentences.zh: 」後從討悅，破之。

translations.literal: " Later he followed in punishing Yue and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Cai You followed in the campaign against Houmochen Yue and helped defeat him.

sentences.zh: 又從迎魏孝武於潼關。

translations.literal: He also followed in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped welcome Emperor Xiaowu of Wei at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，封萇鄉縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: For achievements before and after, he was enfeoffed Baron of Changxiang County, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated service he was enfeoffed Baron of Changxiang County with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統初，加寧朔將軍、羽林監，尋持節、員外散騎常侍，進爵為侯，增邑一千一百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, added General Who Pacifies the North and Captain of the Feathered Forest Guard; soon bearing the staff, Supernumerary Regular Palace Attendant Cavalier, advanced in noble rank to Marquis, fief increased one thousand one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he was made General Who Pacifies the North and captain of the Feathered Forest guard; soon he received staff of authority and the title supernumerary regular palace attendant cavalier, was raised to marquis, and received eleven hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 從太祖擒竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，皆有功，授平東將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shaye—all had merit; granted General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, and fighting at Shaye, earning merit in each; he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 又從太祖戰於河橋，祐乃下馬步鬥，手殺數人。

translations.literal: Again following the Grand Progenitor in fighting at Heqiao, You then dismounted and fought on foot, personally killing several men.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao he again followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai into battle, dismounted, and fought on foot, killing several men himself.

sentences.zh: 左右勸乘馬以備急卒。

translations.literal: Those at his side urged him to mount a horse against sudden attack.
translations.idiomatic: His companions urged him to remount in case of a sudden rush.

sentences.zh: 祐怒曰：「丞相養我如子，今日豈以性命為念！

translations.literal: You angrily said: "The Chancellor raised me like a son—today how could I think of my life!
translations.idiomatic: Cai You snapped: "The Chancellor raised me like a son. Today how could I care about my life!

sentences.zh: 」遂率左右十餘人，齊聲大呼，殺傷甚多。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led more than ten men at his side, all shouting together, and killed and wounded many.
translations.idiomatic: " He then led his dozen or so companions in a great shout and killed or wounded many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵以其無繼，遂圍之十餘重，謂祐曰：「觀君似是勇士，但弛甲來降，豈慮無富貴耶。

translations.literal: The enemy, because he had no reinforcements, thereupon surrounded him more than ten ranks deep and said to You: "Judging by your appearance you seem a brave man—only lay aside your armor and come surrender; why worry that there will be no wealth and honor?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he had no reinforcements, the enemy surrounded him a dozen ranks deep and called out: "You look a brave man. Lay down your armor and surrender—surely wealth and rank await you.

sentences.zh: 」祐罵之曰：「死卒！

translations.literal: " You cursed them, saying: "Dead soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: " Cai You cursed them: "Corpses!

sentences.zh: 吾今取頭，自當封公，何假賊之官號也。

translations.literal: If I take heads today, I shall myself be enfeoffed duke—why borrow the bandits' titles and offices?
translations.idiomatic: If I take heads today I shall win a duke's enfeoffment myself. Why should I borrow titles from rebels?

sentences.zh: 」乃彎弓持滿，四面拒之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon bent his bow to the full and held off the enemy on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: " He strung his bow full and held them off on every side.

sentences.zh: 東魏人弗敢逼，乃募厚甲長刀者，直進取祐。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei men did not dare press close; they then recruited men in heavy armor with long blades to advance straight and take You.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei troops dared not close in; they then picked heavily armored men with long blades to advance straight at Cai You.

sentences.zh: 去祐可三十步，左右勸射之，祐曰：「吾曹性命，在一矢耳，豈虛發哉。

translations.literal: About thirty paces from You, those at his side urged him to shoot; You said: "Our lives all hang on one arrow—how could we shoot in vain?
translations.idiomatic: When the man was about thirty paces away, his companions urged him to shoot. Cai You said: "Our lives hang on this one arrow. How could I waste it?

sentences.zh: 」敵人漸進，可十步，祐乃射之，正中其面，應弦而倒，便以矟刺殺之。

translations.literal: " The enemy gradually advanced; at about ten paces, You then shot him, struck him square in the face, and he fell at the twang of the string; You then stabbed and killed him with his spear.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy drew nearer; at about ten paces Cai You shot, struck him square in the face, and brought him down at the twang of the bowstring, then ran him through with his spear.

sentences.zh: 因此，戰數合，唯失一人。

translations.literal: Because of this, through several rounds of fighting he lost only one man.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting that followed he lost only one man through several engagements.

sentences.zh: 敵乃稍卻。

translations.literal: The enemy then slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 祐徐引退。

translations.literal: You slowly led a withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You slowly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是戰也，我軍不利。

translations.literal: In this battle, our army was not favored.
translations.idiomatic: In that battle our army had the worse of it.

sentences.zh: 太祖已還。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor had already returned.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai had already withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 祐至弘農，夜中與太祖相會。

translations.literal: You reached Hongnong and in the middle of the night met the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You reached Hongnong and met Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in the middle of the night.

sentences.zh: 太祖見祐至，字之曰：「承先，爾來，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, seeing You arrive, addressed him by style and said: "Chengxian, you have come—I have no worry left.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai saw Cai You arrive he called him by style and said: "Chengxian, you have come. I have nothing left to fear.

sentences.zh: 」太祖心驚，不得寢，枕祐股上，乃安。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor's heart was startled and he could not sleep; he rested his head on You's thigh and only then was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " His heart was still shaken and he could not sleep until he laid his head on Cai You's thigh and at last found rest.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵為公，增邑三百戶，授京兆郡守。

translations.literal: For merit advanced in noble rank to Duke, fief increased three hundred households, granted Administrator of Jingzhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was raised to duke with three hundred additional households and made administrator of Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 九年，東魏〔北〕豫州刺史高仲密舉州來附。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Eastern Wei [Northern] Yuzhou Governor Gao Zhongmi offered the province in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Gao Zhongmi, governor of Northern Yuzhou under Eastern Wei, surrendered his province.

sentences.zh: 太祖率軍援之，與齊神武遇，戰於邙山。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor led troops to aid him, met Qi Shenwu, and fought at Mount Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched to support him, met Gao Huan, and fought at Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 祐時著明光鐵鎧，所向無前。

translations.literal: You at the time wore bright iron armor and wherever he went none could stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You wore bright iron armor and cut through every enemy line before him.

sentences.zh: 敵人咸曰「此是鐵猛獸也」，皆遽避之。

translations.literal: The enemy all said, "This is an iron beast," and all hastily avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy all cried, "That is an iron beast," and hurried out of his way.

sentences.zh: 俄授青州刺史，轉原州刺史，加帥都督，尋除大都督。

translations.literal: Soon granted Governor of Qing Province, transferred to Governor of Yuan Province, added commandery area commander, soon removed [from current post] and made Grand Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Qing Province, then transferred to governor of Yuan Province with commandery area commander added, and soon promoted to grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遭父憂，請終喪紀。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he suffered his father's mourning and requested to complete the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when his father died, he asked to observe the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 弗許。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中，賜姓大利稽氏，進爵懷寧郡公。

translations.literal: Transferred to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Three Departments, added Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Opening Office with Equal in Three Departments, Palace Attendant, granted the surname Dali Ji, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Huaining commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in three departments, then given the added titles grand general of fast cavalry, opening office with equal in three departments, and palace attendant; he received the surname Dali Ji and was raised to Duke of Huaining commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，中領軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he served as central army commander.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授兵部中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, granted Middle Grand Master of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established he was made middle grand master of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 江陵初附，諸蠻騷動，詔祐與大將軍豆盧寧討平之。

translations.literal: When Jiangling had just submitted, the various Man tribes were in turmoil; an edict ordered You together with Grand General Dou Lu Ning to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling had just submitted and the barbarian tribes were in turmoil, an edict sent Cai You with Grand General Dou Lu Ning to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜大將軍，給後部鼓吹。

translations.literal: In the third year, appointed Grand General, granted rear guard musical instruments.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made grand general and granted rear-guard musical instruments.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，增邑幷前四千戶，別封一子縣伯。

translations.literal: For achievements before and after, fief increased together with previous to four thousand households; one son separately enfeoffed County Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated service his fief was raised to four thousand households in all, and one son was separately enfeoffed as county marquis.

sentences.zh: 太祖不豫，祐與晉公護、賀蘭祥等侍疾。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor was ill, You together with Duke of Jin Hu, Helan Xiang, and others attended his sickness.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai fell ill, Cai You attended him together with Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, Helan Xiang, and others.

sentences.zh: 及太祖崩，祐悲慕不已，遂得氣疾。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor died, You grieved and longed without cease and thereupon contracted a breathing ailment.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai died, Cai You grieved without end and contracted a breathing ailment.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜少保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, appointed Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Cai You was made junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 祐與尉遲綱俱掌禁兵，遞直殿省。

translations.literal: You together with Yuchi Gang both held the forbidden troops and alternated duty in the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You and Yuchi Gang jointly commanded the palace guard and took turns on duty in the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 時帝信任司會李植等，謀害晉公護，祐每泣諫，帝不聽。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor trusted Director of Justice Li Zhi and others, plotting to harm Duke of Jin Hu; You each time wept and remonstrated, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then trusted Director of Justice Li Zhi and others in a plot against Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu; Cai You wept and remonstrated again and again, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 尋而帝廢。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the emperor was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor was deposed.

sentences.zh: 世宗卽位，拜小司馬，少保如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, appointed Junior Minister of War, Junior Preceptor as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Cai You was made junior minister of war while retaining the post of junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 帝之為公子也，與祐特相友昵，至是禮遇彌隆。

translations.literal: When the emperor had been a prince, he and You were especially friendly and intimate; now his courtesy and favor were even greater.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had been a prince he and Cai You had been especially close; now his favor was even greater.

sentences.zh: 御膳每有異味，輒輟以賜祐；

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial meal had special delicacies, he would set them aside and bestow them on You;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the imperial table had special delicacies, the emperor would set them aside for Cai You;

sentences.zh: 羣臣朝宴，每被別留，或至昏夜，列炬鳴笳，送祐還宅。

translations.literal: at court banquets with the assembled ministers, You was always kept behind separately, sometimes until dusk; lines of torches and blaring pipes saw You home.
translations.idiomatic: at court banquets he always kept Cai You behind after the others, sometimes until nightfall, and sent him home with lines of torches and blaring pipes.

sentences.zh: 祐以過蒙禮遇，常辭疾避之。

translations.literal: You, because he received excessive courtesy and favor, often pleaded illness to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You, feeling he received more honor than he deserved, often pleaded illness to keep his distance.

sentences.zh: 至於婚姻，尤不願交於勢要。

translations.literal: As for marriage, he especially did not wish to ally with the powerful and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: In marriage above all he refused ties with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官權鎮原州。

translations.literal: Soon by his original office he was made provisional garrison commander of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made provisional garrison commander of Yuan Province in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 頃之，授

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed

translations.literal: (Xuan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yi]

sentences.zh: 〔宜〕州刺史，未之部，因先氣疾動，卒於原州。

translations.literal: [Yi] Province Governor; he never took up the post, but his old ailment returned and he died at Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: governor of Yi Province. He had not yet reported to his post when his old ailment returned and he died at Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 時年五十四。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 祐少有大志，與鄉人李穆，布衣齊名。

translations.literal: You from youth had great ambition; with his fellow townsman Li Mu, in plain clothes they were equally famed.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Cai You had high ambition; he and his fellow townsman Li Mu were equally famed while still in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 嘗相謂曰：「大丈夫當建立功名，以取富貴，安能久處貧賤邪！

translations.literal: They once said to each other: "A great man should establish merit and fame to win wealth and honor—how can he long remain in poverty and low station!
translations.idiomatic: They once said to each other: "A true man should win fame and fortune through achievement. How can he linger forever in poverty and obscurity?

sentences.zh: 」言訖，各大笑。

translations.literal: " When the words were finished, each laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " When they had finished speaking, both laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 穆卽申公也。

translations.literal: Mu was Duke of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu was Duke of Shen.

sentences.zh: 後皆如其言。

translations.literal: Later both were as their words said.
translations.idiomatic: Later both fulfilled what they had said.

sentences.zh: 及從征伐，常潰圍陷陣，為士卒先。

translations.literal: When he followed on campaigns and suppressions, he often broke through encirclement and stormed formations, going before the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he often broke through encirclements and led the charge ahead of his men.

sentences.zh: 軍還之日，諸將爭功，祐終無所競。

translations.literal: On the day the army returned, the various generals competed for merit; You to the end made no claim.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, the generals all wrangled over credit; Cai You never joined the contest.

sentences.zh: 太祖

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai

translations.literal: (nai)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: nai]

sentences.zh: 〔每〕歎之，嘗謂諸將曰：「承先口不言勳，孤當代其論敘。

translations.literal: [mei] sighed over him, and once said to the generals: "Chengxian never speaks of merit; I myself shall relate his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He always sighed over this and once told the generals: "Chengxian never speaks of his merits—I shall state them for him.

sentences.zh: 」其見知如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 性節儉，所得祿皆散與宗族，身死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal; the salary he received he always distributed to his clan; on the day he died, the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, he gave all his salary to his clan; when he died, his household had nothing left.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、柱國大將軍、大都督、五州諸軍事、原州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted commissioner with full credentials, pillar grand general, supreme area commander, commander-in-chief of military affairs in five provinces, and governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made commissioner with full credentials, pillar grand general, supreme area commander, commander-in-chief of military affairs in five provinces, and governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhuang (Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 子正嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 官至使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He rose to commissioner with full credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to commissioner with full credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 祐弟澤，頗好學，有幹能。

translations.literal: You's younger brother Ze was quite fond of learning and had ability in practical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You's younger brother Ze was quite fond of learning and capable in practical affairs.

sentences.zh: 起家魏廣平王參軍、丞相府兼記室，加宣

translations.literal: He began his career as aide to the Prince of Guangping of Wei and concurrent recorder in the grand chancellor's office, with added General Who Establishes
translations.idiomatic: He began as aide to the Prince of Guangping of Wei and concurrent recorder in the grand chancellor's office, with added General Who Establishes

translations.literal: (Wu)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Wu]

sentences.zh: 〔威〕將軍、給事中。

translations.literal: [wei] Might and palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Might and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 從尉遲迥平蜀，授帥都督，賜爵安彌縣男。

translations.literal: Following Yuchi Jiong in pacifying Shu, he was appointed commander-in-chief and granted noble rank as Baron of Anmi county.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yuchi Jiong in pacifying Shu, he was made commander-in-chief and enfeoffed Baron of Anmi county.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司輅下大夫、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、澧州刺史。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted to junior grand master of the carriage office, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through junior grand master of the carriage office, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Li Province.

sentences.zh: 在州受賂，總管代王達以其功臣子弟，密奏貰之。

translations.literal: While in the province he accepted bribes; the area commander Prince Dai Wang Da, because he was a meritorious minister's son, secretly memorialized to pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: While governing the province he took bribes; area commander Prince Dai Wang Da, because Ze was a meritorious minister's son, secretly memorialized to pardon him.

sentences.zh: 後為

translations.literal: Later he was made
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made

translations.literal: (Mang)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Mang]

sentences.zh: ［鄖］州刺史，不從司馬消難，被害。

translations.literal: [Yun] provincial governor; he would not follow Sima Xiaonan and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: governor of Yun Province; he refused to follow Sima Xiaonan and was killed.

sentences.zh: 常善，高陽人也。

translations.literal: Chang Shan was a man of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shan was a native of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 世為豪族。

translations.literal: His family for generations were a powerful clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had for generations been a powerful clan.

sentences.zh: 父安成，魏正光末，茹茹寇邊，以統軍從鎮將慕容勝與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: His father Ancheng — at the end of Zhengguang of Wei, when the Ruru raided the border, as army commander he followed garrison general Murong Sheng into battle and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ancheng — at the end of Zhengguang, when the Ruru raided the frontier, served as army commander under garrison general Murong Sheng and routed them.

sentences.zh: 時破六汗拔陵作亂，欲逼安成。

translations.literal: At the time Poliuhan Baling rebelled and wished to coerce Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Poliuhan Baling rebelled, he tried to force Ancheng to join him.

sentences.zh: 不從，乃率所部討陵。

translations.literal: He refused, and thereupon led his command to attack Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Ancheng refused and led his troops against Baling.

sentences.zh: 以功授伏波將軍，給鼓節。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted General Who Subdues Waves and drums and batons of authority.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made General Who Subdues Waves and given drums and batons of authority.

sentences.zh: 後與拔陵連戰，卒於陣。

translations.literal: Later he fought repeatedly with Baling and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He later fought Baling again and again and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 善，魏孝昌中，從爾朱榮入洛，授威烈將軍、都督，加龍驤將軍、中散大夫、直寢，封房城縣男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Shan — in the Xiaochang era of Wei, he followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang, was granted General of Majestic Might and area commander; added Dragon Charger General, palace secretary, and directly-attending guard; enfeoffed as Baron of Fangcheng county, fief three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shan — in the Xiaochang era he followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang, was made General of Majestic Might and area commander, given Dragon Charger General, palace secretary, and directly-attending guard, and enfeoffed Baron of Fangcheng county with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後從太祖平侯莫陳悅，除天水郡守。

translations.literal: Later he followed Grand Progenitor in pacifying Houmochen Yue and was made administrator of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in defeating Houmochen Yue and was made administrator of Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，授武衛將軍，進爵武始縣伯，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he was granted General Who Guards the Army, advanced in noble rank to Earl of Wushi county, fief increased two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, he was made General Who Guards the Army, raised to Earl of Wushi county, and given two hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 大統初，加平東將軍，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, added General Who Pacifies the East, advanced in noble rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong he was given General Who Pacifies the East and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 擒竇泰，復弘農，破沙苑，累有戰功。

translations.literal: Capturing Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, breaking Shaye — repeatedly distinguished in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battle of Shaye, winning distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 除使持節、衛將軍，假驃騎大將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Appointed commissioner with full credentials, Guard General, acting grand general of rapid cavalry, and governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commissioner with full credentials, Guard General, acting grand general of rapid cavalry, and governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 四年，從戰河橋，加大都督，進爵為公，除涇州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he followed the battle at Heqiao, was promoted to grand area commander, advanced in noble rank to duke, and made governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he fought at Heqiao, was promoted to grand area commander, raised to duke, and made governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 屬茹茹入寇，抄掠北邊，善率所部破之，盡獲所掠。

translations.literal: When the Ruru invaded and raided the northern border, Shan led his command and defeated them, fully recovering what had been looted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ruru raided the northern frontier, Chang Shan led his troops against them, defeated them, and recovered everything they had taken.

sentences.zh: 拜車騎大將軍、儀同三司，遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，西安州刺史。

translations.literal: Granted grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-to-three-division protocol; transferred to grand general of rapid cavalry, opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and governor of Xi'an Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol, then transferred to grand general of rapid cavalry with opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol and governor of Xi'an Province.

sentences.zh: 轉蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 頻蒞三蕃，頗有政績。

translations.literal: Repeatedly taking charge of three border regions, he had considerable administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly held three frontier posts and won a solid record of governance.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，進爵永陽郡公，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Yongyang commandery, fief increased two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was raised to Duke of Yongyang commandery and given two thousand additional households.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜大將軍、寧州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, granted grand general and area commander of Ning Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, he was made grand general and area commander of Ning Province.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，入為小司徒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he entered court as Junior Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding he entered court as Junior Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 四年，突厥出師與隋公楊忠東伐，令善應接之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Turks marched out together with Duke of Sui Yang Zhong on an eastern campaign; he ordered Shan to meet and support them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Turks marched out with Duke of Sui Yang Zhong on an eastern campaign, and the court ordered Chang Shan to meet and support them.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year he died, age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the fifth year, aged sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、柱國大將軍、大都督、延夏鹽恆燕五州諸軍事、延州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted commissioner with full credentials, pillar grand general, supreme area commander, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yan, Xia, Salt, Heng, and Yan provinces, and governor of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made commissioner with full credentials, pillar grand general, supreme area commander, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yan, Xia, Salt, Heng, and Yan provinces, and governor of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 子升和嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shenghe succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shenghe succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 先以善勳，拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: Earlier, because of Shan's merit, granted equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because of Chang Shan's merit, he had been granted equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 辛威，隴西人也。

translations.literal: Xin Wei was a man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Wei was a native of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 祖大汗，魏渭州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dahan was governor of Wei Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dahan was governor of Wei Province.

sentences.zh: 父生，河州四面大都督。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was supreme area commander of the four circuits of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng was supreme area commander of the four circuits of He Province.

sentences.zh: 及威著勳，追贈大將軍、涼甘等五州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wei won distinction, his forebears were posthumously granted grand general and governors of the five provinces of Liang, Gan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Wei won distinction, his forebears were posthumously made grand general and governors of Liang, Gan, and three other provinces.

sentences.zh: 威少慷慨，有志略。

translations.literal: Wei from youth was generous and high-minded, with ambition and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Wei from youth was generous and high-minded, with ambition and strategy.

sentences.zh: 初從賀拔岳征討有功，假輔國將軍、都督。

translations.literal: At first he followed He Ba Yue on punitive campaigns with merit; granted acting General Who Assists the State and area commander.
translations.idiomatic: At first he followed He Ba Yue on punitive campaigns with distinction and was made acting General Who Assists the State and area commander.

sentences.zh: 及太祖統岳之衆，見威奇之，引為帳內。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor took command of Yue's army, seeing Wei was extraordinary, he brought him into his personal staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai took command of He Ba Yue's army, struck by Xin Wei's talent, he brought him into his personal staff.

sentences.zh: 尋授羽林監，封白土縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Soon granted Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, enfeoffed as Earl of Baitu county, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and enfeoffed Earl of Baitu county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從迎魏孝武，因攻回洛城，功居最。

translations.literal: Following in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he also attacked Huiluo city; his merit ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei he also attacked Huiluo city, and his merit ranked foremost.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，拜寧遠將軍，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, granted General of Distant Pacification, fief increased two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he was made General of Distant Pacification and given two hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 累遷通直散騎常侍，進爵為侯，增邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to regular palace attendant of the scattered cavalry, advanced in noble rank to marquis, fief increased three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to regular palace attendant of the scattered cavalry, was raised to marquis, and given three hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，並先鋒陷敵，勇冠一時。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Dou Tai, recovery of Hongnong, and battle at Shaye — all as vanguard breaking the enemy; his courage topped his age.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battle of Shaye he led the vanguard and broke the enemy; his courage topped his age.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，授撫軍將軍、銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For achievements before and after, granted General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated service he was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of the Silver Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 從于謹破襄城。

translations.literal: Following Yu Jin in breaking Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yu Jin in the capture of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 又從獨孤信入洛陽，經河橋陣，加持節，進爵為公，增邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Again following Dugu Xin into Luoyang, passing through the Heqiao battle line, granted enhanced credentials, advanced in noble rank to duke, fief increased eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Dugu Xin into Luoyang, fought at the Heqiao line, was granted enhanced credentials, raised to duke, and given eight hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 五年，授揚州刺史，加大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, granted governor of Yang Province and promoted to grand area commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made governor of Yang Province and promoted to grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司，驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，賜姓普

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-to-three-division protocol; grand general of rapid cavalry and opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol; granted surname Pu
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry with equal-to-three-division protocol and grand general of rapid cavalry with opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol, and granted the surname Pu

translations.literal: (Mao)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Mao]

sentences.zh: 〔屯〕氏，出為鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: [Tun] clan, sent out as governor of Fu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tun clan, and sent out as governor of Fu Province.

sentences.zh: 威時望旣重，朝廷以桑梓榮之，遷河州刺史，本州大中正。

translations.literal: Wei's standing in his time was already weighty; the court honored his native place and transferred him to governor of He Province and grand chancellor of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Wei's standing was already great; the court honored his native place by making him governor of He Province and grand chancellor of his home province.

sentences.zh: 頻領二鎮，頗得民和。

translations.literal: Repeatedly holding two commands, he quite won the people to harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Holding two commands in succession, he won the people to harmony.

sentences.zh: 威性持重，有威嚴。

translations.literal: Wei by nature was steady and weighty, with dignity and sternness.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Wei was steady and weighty by nature, with dignity and sternness.

sentences.zh: 歷官數十年，未嘗有過，故得以身名終。

translations.literal: Holding office for several decades, he never had a fault; thus he was able to end with body and name intact.
translations.idiomatic: He held office for decades without a fault and so ended with reputation and life intact.

sentences.zh: 兼其家門友義，五世同居，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: Together with the friendly righteousness of his household — five generations dwelling together — the world praised this.
translations.idiomatic: His household was noted for friendly righteousness — five generations under one roof — and the world praised them for it.

sentences.zh: 子永達嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yongda succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongda succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 大象末，以威勳，拜儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, because of Wei's merit, granted equal-to-three-division grand general.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang, because of Xin Wei's merit, he was made equal-to-three-division grand general.

sentences.zh: 厙狄昌字恃德，神武人也。

translations.literal: Shedichang, styled Shide, was a man of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Shedichang, styled Shide, was a native of Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 少便騎射，有膂力。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at mounted archery and had physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was skilled at mounted archery and possessed great strength.

sentences.zh: 及長，進止閒雅，膽氣壯烈，每以將帥自許。

translations.literal: When grown, his conduct and bearing were refined and easy, his courage and spirit fierce; he often considered himself fit to be a general.
translations.idiomatic: When grown his bearing was refined and easy and his courage fierce; he often considered himself fit to be a general.

sentences.zh: 年十八，爾朱天光引為幢主，加討夷將軍。

translations.literal: At age eighteen, Erzhu Tiangguang brought him in as standard-bearer chief, with added title General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen Erzhu Tiangguang took him on as standard-bearer chief and gave him the added title General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 從天光定關中，以功拜寧遠將軍、奉車都尉、統軍。

translations.literal: Following Tiangguang in pacifying Guanzhong, for merit granted General of Distant Pacification, chariot commander of the court, and army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Following Tiangguang in pacifying Guanzhong, he was rewarded with General of Distant Pacification, chariot commander of the court, and army commander.

sentences.zh: 天光敗，又從賀拔岳。

translations.literal: When Tiangguang was defeated, he again followed He Ba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiangguang was defeated, he again followed He Ba Yue.

sentences.zh: 授征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Granted General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General Who Conquers the West and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 及岳被害，昌與諸將議翊戴太祖。

translations.literal: When Yue was murdered, Chang together with the generals deliberated supporting Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ba Yue was murdered, Shedichang with the other generals deliberated supporting Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 從平侯莫陳悅，賜爵陰盤縣子，加衛將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following in pacifying Houmochen Yue, granted noble rank as Viscount of Yinpan county, with added Guard General and Right Grand Master of the Honorific Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Following Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in defeating Houmochen Yue, he was enfeoffed Viscount of Yinpan county and given Guard General and Right Grand Master of the Honorific Seal.

sentences.zh: 後從太祖迎魏孝武，復潼關，改封長子縣子，邑八百戶。

translations.literal: Later following Grand Progenitor in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, recovering Tong Pass, changed enfeoffment to Viscount of Changzi county, fief eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and recovering Tong Pass, he was re-enfeoffed Viscount of Changzi county with a fief of eight hundred households.

sentences.zh: 大統初，進爵為公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, advanced in noble rank to duke, fief increased one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong he was raised to duke and given one thousand additional households.

sentences.zh: 從破竇泰，授車騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following the defeat of Dou Tai, granted grand general of chariots and cavalry and Left Grand Master of the Honorific Seal.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat of Dou Tai he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and Left Grand Master of the Honorific Seal.

sentences.zh: 又從復弘農，戰沙苑，昌皆先登陷陣。

translations.literal: Again following the recovery of Hongnong and battle at Shaye — Chang each time was first to ascend and break the line.
translations.idiomatic: He again fought in the recovery of Hongnong and the battle of Shaye; each time Shedichang was first over the wall and broke the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，授帥都督。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor commended him and granted commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai commended him and made him commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四年，從戰河橋，除冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, following the battle at Heqiao, made governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after fighting at Heqiao, he was made governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 後與于謹破胡賊劉平伏於上郡，授馮翊郡守。

translations.literal: Later together with Yu Jin he defeated the Hu bandit Liu Pingfu at Shang commandery; granted administrator of Fengyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Yu Jin, he defeated the Hu bandit Liu Pingfu at Shang commandery and was made administrator of Fengyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉河北郡守。

translations.literal: After some time, transferred to administrator of Hebei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to administrator of Hebei commandery.

sentences.zh: 十三年，錄前後功，授大都督、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, recording achievements before and after, granted grand area commander and regular palace attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, for his accumulated service, he was made grand area commander and regular palace attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又從隨公楊忠破蠻賊田社清，昌功為最，增邑三百戶，拜儀同三司。
