translations.literal: Again following Duke of Sui Yang Zhong in defeating the Man bandit Tian Sheqing — Chang's achievement ranked foremost; fief increased three hundred households, granted equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Again following Duke of Sui Yang Zhong against the Man bandit Tian Sheqing, Shedichang's achievement ranked foremost; he received three hundred additional households and equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 尋遷開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to opening-office equal-to-three-division protocol.

sentences.zh: 十六年，出為東夏州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, sent out as governor of East Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was sent out as governor of East Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，進爵方城郡公，增邑幷前四千一百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Fangcheng commandery; fief increased together with previous to four thousand one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was raised to Duke of Fangcheng commandery, with a combined fief of four thousand one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授稍伯中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, granted Junior Suibo Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established, he was made Junior Suibo Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, granted grand general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 田弘字廣略，高平人也。

translations.literal: Tian Hong, styled Guanglue, was a man of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hong, styled Guanglue, was a native of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 少慷慨，志立功名，膂力過人，敢勇有謀略。

translations.literal: In youth he was generous, aspired to establish fame and merit; his physical strength surpassed others and he was daring, brave, and strategic.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was generous and aspired to win fame and merit; his strength surpassed others and he was daring, brave, and strategic.

sentences.zh: 魏永安中，陷於万俟醜奴。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era of Wei he was captured by Wanqij Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was captured by Wanqij Chounu.

sentences.zh: 爾朱天光入關，弘自原州歸順，授都督。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Tiangguang entered the Pass, Hong came from Yuan Province to submit, and was granted area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Tiangguang entered the Pass, Tian Hong came from Yuan Province to submit and was made area commander.

sentences.zh: 及太祖初統衆，弘求謁見，乃論世事，深被引納，卽處以爪牙之任。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor first took command of the army, Hong requested an audience; he thereupon discussed current affairs and was deeply taken into confidence, immediately placed in a claw-and-fang role.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai first took command of the army, Tian Hong asked for an audience, discussed current affairs, and was deeply taken into confidence and immediately placed in a trusted fighting role.

sentences.zh: 又以迎魏孝武功，封鶉陰縣子，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Also for the merit of welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, enfeoffed as Viscount of Chunyin county, fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Also for the merit of welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was enfeoffed Viscount of Chunyin county with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太祖常以所著鐵甲賜弘云：「天下若定，還將此甲示孤也。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor often bestowed upon Hong the iron armor he had worn, saying: "If the realm is settled, return and show this armor to me.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai often gave Tian Hong the iron armor he himself had worn, saying: "If the realm is settled, bring this armor back and show it to me.

sentences.zh: 」大統三年，轉帥都督，進爵為公。

translations.literal: " In the third year of Datong, transferred to area commander, advanced in noble rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year of Datong he was made area commander and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 從太祖復弘農，戰沙苑，解洛陽圍，破河橋陣，弘功居多，累蒙殊賞，賜姓紇幹氏。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor in recovering Hongnong, fighting at Shaye, relieving the siege of Luoyang, and breaking the Heqiao formation—Hong's merit was greatest; he repeatedly received special rewards and was granted the surname Hegegan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in recovering Hongnong, fought at Shaye, lifted the siege of Luoyang, and broke the Heqiao line; Tian Hong's merit stood foremost. He received repeated special rewards and was granted the surname Hegegan.

sentences.zh: 尋授原州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon appointed governor of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 以弘勳望兼至，故以衣錦榮之。

translations.literal: Because Hong's achievements and reputation were both lofty, he was honored with return in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tian Hong's record and standing were both high, he was honored with a triumphant return to his home region.

sentences.zh: 太祖在同州，文武並集，乃謂之曰：「人人如弘盡心，天下豈不早定。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was at Tong Province with civil and military officials all assembled; he said to them: "If every man were as devoted as Hong, would not the realm be settled early?
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was at Tong Province with civil and military officials gathered, he told them: "If every man served as wholeheartedly as Tian Hong, would the realm not be settled already?

sentences.zh: 」卽授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-in-three-departments.
translations.idiomatic: " He was thereupon made grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-in-three-departments.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei, given the added rank of grand general of fast cavalry and opening-office equal-in-three-departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was given the added ranks of grand general of fast cavalry and opening-office equal-in-three-departments.

sentences.zh: 平蜀之後，梁信州刺史蕭韶等各據所部，未從朝化，詔弘討平之。

translations.literal: After Shu was pacified, Liang's Xizhou governor Xiao Shao and others each held their districts and had not yet submitted to the court; an edict ordered Hong to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified, Liang Xizhou governor Xiao Shao and others still held their territories and had not accepted the court's rule; an edict ordered Tian Hong to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 又討西平叛羌及鳳州叛氐等，並破之。

translations.literal: He also suppressed the rebel Qiang of Xiping and the rebel Di of Feng Province, and defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: He also put down the rebel Qiang of Xiping and the rebel Di of Feng Province, defeating them all.

sentences.zh: 弘每臨陣，摧鋒直前，身被一百餘箭，破骨者九，馬被十矟，朝廷壯之。

translations.literal: Whenever Hong went into battle he smashed the vanguard head-on; his body took more than a hundred arrows, with nine breaking bone; his horse took ten spears—the court admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tian Hong entered battle he charged straight through the enemy van; his body took more than a hundred arrows, nine of them breaking bone, and his horse ten spears—the court admired him.

sentences.zh: 信州羣蠻反，又詔弘與賀若敦等平之。

translations.literal: The various tribes of Xin rebelled; again an edict ordered Hong with He Ruo Dun and others to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes of Xin rebelled, an edict again ordered Tian Hong, with He Ruo Dun and others, to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵鴈門郡公，邑通前二千七百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Yanmen Commandery, fief together with previous two thousand seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, Tian Hong was raised to Duke of Yanmen Commandery with a combined fief of two thousand seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，陳湘州刺史華皎來附，弘從衛公直赴援。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, Chen Xiangzhou governor Hua Jiao came over to submit; Hong followed Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe, Chen Xiangzhou governor Hua Jiao surrendered; Tian Hong followed Duke of Wei Yuwen Zhi to the relief.

sentences.zh: 與陳人戰，不利，仍以弘為江陵總管。

translations.literal: In battle with the Chen forces they were unsuccessful; Hong was nevertheless kept as inspector-general of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The battle with Chen went badly, but Tian Hong was nevertheless kept on as inspector-general of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 及陳將吳明徹來寇，弘與梁主蕭巋退保

translations.literal: When Chen general Wu Mingche came to raid, Hong with Liang ruler Xiao Kui withdrew to hold
translations.idiomatic: When Chen general Wu Mingche invaded, Tian Hong and Liang ruler Xiao Kui withdrew to hold

translations.literal: (Zong)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Zong]

sentences.zh: 〔紀〕南，令副總管高琳拒守，明徹退，乃還江陵。

translations.literal: [Ji] south; he ordered deputy inspector-general Gao Lin to hold defense; Mingche withdrew, then they returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan, had deputy inspector-general Gao Lin hold the defense; Mingche withdrew, and they returned to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 尋以弘為仁壽城主，以逼宜陽。

translations.literal: Soon Hong was made commandant of Renshou fortress to press Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Tian Hong was made commandant of Renshou fortress to press Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 齊將段孝先、斛律明月出軍定隴以為宜陽援，弘與陳公純破之，遂拔宜陽等九城。

translations.literal: Qi generals Duan Xiaoxian and Hulü Mingyue led troops from Dinglong as relief for Yiyang; Hong with Duke of Chen Yuwen Chun defeated them and then took nine cities including Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi generals Duan Xiaoxian and Hulü Mingyue marched from Dinglong to relieve Yiyang; Tian Hong and Duke of Chen Yuwen Chun defeated them and took nine cities, including Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 以功增邑五百戶，進位柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: For merit his fief was increased five hundred households and he was advanced to pillar-of-state grand general.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit his fief was increased by five hundred households and he was raised to pillar-of-state grand general.

sentences.zh: 子恭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Gong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 少有名譽，早歷顯位。

translations.literal: From youth he had a fine reputation; early he passed through prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Gong had a fine reputation from youth and rose early to prominent posts.

sentences.zh: 大象末，位至柱國、小司馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he reached pillar of state and lesser master of the horse.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daxiang era he had reached pillar of state and lesser master of the horse.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又追錄弘勳，進恭爵觀國公。

translations.literal: The court again recorded Hong's achievements posthumously and advanced Gong's noble rank to Duke of Guan State.
translations.idiomatic: The court again recorded Tian Hong's achievements posthumously and raised Gong to Duke of Guan State.

sentences.zh: 梁椿字千年，代人也。

translations.literal: Liang Chun, styled Qiannian, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chun, styled Qiannian, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖屈朱，魏昌平鎮將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quzhu was Wei garrison commander of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quzhu had been garrison commander of Changping under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父提，內

translations.literal: His father Ti, Inner
translations.idiomatic: His father Ti served as inner

translations.literal: (Correct)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: zheng]

sentences.zh: 郎。

translations.literal: Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: attendant.

sentences.zh: 椿初以統軍從爾朱榮入洛，復從榮破葛榮於滏口，以軍功進授都將。

translations.literal: Chun at first as commander followed Erzhu Rong into Luoyang; again following Rong he broke Ge Rong at Fekou and for military merit was advanced and appointed division commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chun first entered Luoyang as a commander under Erzhu Rong; he followed Rong again in the defeat of Ge Rong at Fekou and, for military merit, was promoted to division commandant.

sentences.zh: 後從賀拔岳討平万俟醜奴、蕭寶夤等，遷中堅將軍、屯騎校尉、子都督。

translations.literal: Later following He Ba Yue he suppressed and pacified Wanqidu Chounu, Xiao Baoyin, and others; transferred to general of the middle firm army, colonel of the garrison cavalry, and sub-area commander.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under He Ba Yue, he helped suppress Wanqidu Chounu, Xiao Baoyin, and others; he was made general of the middle firm army, colonel of the garrison cavalry, and sub-area commander.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，拜征西將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, appointed general pacifying the west and grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai he was appointed general pacifying the west and grand master of the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 二年，除高平郡守，封盧奴縣男，邑一百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year, removed [from current post] and made administrator of Gaoping commandery, enfeoffed Baron of Lunu County, fief one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made administrator of Gaoping commandery and enfeoffed Baron of Lunu County with a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太昌元年，進授都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang, advanced and appointed area commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taichang he was promoted to area commander.

sentences.zh: 從太祖平侯莫陳悅，拜衛將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Progenitor in pacifying Houmochen Yue, appointed general of the guard and right grand master of splendid wealth.
translations.idiomatic: After following Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in defeating Houmochen Yue, he was made general of the guard and right grand master of splendid wealth.

sentences.zh: 大統初，進爵欒城縣伯，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, advanced in noble rank to Earl of Luancheng County, fief increased five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he was raised to Earl of Luancheng County with five hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 出為隴東郡守。

translations.literal: Sent out as administrator of Longdong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as administrator of Longdong commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋進爵為公，增邑五百戶，遷梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon advanced in noble rank to duke, fief increased five hundred households, transferred to governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to duke with five hundred more households and transferred to governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 從復弘農，戰沙苑，與獨孤信入洛陽，從宇文貴破東魏將堯雄等，累有戰功。

translations.literal: Following in recovering Hongnong, fighting at Shaye, entering Luoyang with Dugu Xin, following Yuwen Gui in breaking Eastern Wei general Yao Xiong and others—repeatedly had battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the recovery of Hongnong and at Shaye, entered Luoyang with Dugu Xin, and under Yuwen Gui defeated Eastern Wei general Yao Xiong and others, earning repeated distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 授車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督。

translations.literal: Appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-in-three-departments, and grand area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-in-three-departments, and grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 從戰河橋，進爵東平郡公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Following in battle at Heqiao, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Dongping Commandery, fief increased one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Heqiao and was raised to Duke of Dongping Commandery with one thousand additional households.

sentences.zh: 俄遷侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to palace attendant, grand general of fast cavalry, and opening-office equal-in-three-departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to palace attendant, grand general of fast cavalry, and opening-office equal-in-three-departments.

sentences.zh: 七年，從于謹討稽胡劉平伏，椿擒其別帥劉持塞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, following Yu Jin in suppressing the Ji Hu Liu Pingfu, Chun captured his secondary commander Liu Chisai.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed Yu Jin against the Ji Hu Liu Pingfu and captured Liu's lieutenant Liu Chisai.

sentences.zh: 又從獨孤信討岷州羌梁仚定，破之。

translations.literal: Again following Dugu Xin in suppressing the Minzhou Qiang Liang Xianding, he defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Dugu Xin against the Minzhou Qiang Liang Xianding and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 除清州刺史。

translations.literal: Removed [from current post] and made governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 在州雖無他政績，而夷夏安之。

translations.literal: In the province though he had no other administrative achievements, barbarians and Chinese were both at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he had no other notable administrative record, yet barbarians and Chinese alike lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從李弼赴潁川援侯景。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, following Li Bi in going to Yingchuan to aid Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he followed Li Bi to Yingchuan to aid Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 別攻閻韓鎮，斬其鎮城徐衛。

translations.literal: Separately attacked Yanhan garrison and beheaded its garrison commander Xu Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On a separate attack he took Yanhan garrison and beheaded its commander Xu Wei.

sentences.zh: 城主卜貴洛率軍士千人降。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Bu Guiluo led one thousand soldiers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Bu Guiluo surrendered with one thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 以功增邑四百戶。

translations.literal: For merit fief increased four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit his fief was increased by four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，除華州刺史，改封清陵郡公，增邑通前三千七百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, removed [from current post] and made governor of Hua Province, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Qingling Commandery, fief together with previous three thousand seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, Liang Chun was made governor of Hua Province, given the title Duke of Qingling Commandery, and granted a combined fief of three thousand seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年，入為少保，轉少傅。

translations.literal: In the second year, entered [the capital] as junior preceptor, transferred to junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he entered court as junior preceptor, then became junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, appointed grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 卒於位。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈恆鄜延丹寧五州諸軍事，行恆州刺史，諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted overall command of military affairs for Heng, Fen, Yan, Dan, and Ning provinces, acting governor of Heng, posthumous title Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted overall command of military affairs for Heng, Fen, Yan, Dan, and Ning provinces, with acting authority as governor of Heng, and given the posthumous title Lie.

sentences.zh: 椿性果毅，善於撫納，所獲賞物，分賜麾下，故每踐敵場，咸得其死力。

translations.literal: Chun by nature was resolute and firm, skilled at soothing and accepting men; whatever reward goods he obtained he distributed to his subordinates, so whenever he entered the enemy field they all gave him their utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chun was resolute by nature and skilled at winning men over; he shared every reward with his subordinates, so on every battlefield they fought to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 雅好儉素，不營貲產，時論以此稱焉。

translations.literal: By refined taste he loved simplicity, did not amass property—the men of the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly by choice and amassed no wealth, and men of the age praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子明，魏恭帝二年，以椿功襲爵豐陽縣公。

translations.literal: His son Ming—in the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, for Chun's merit inherited the noble rank as Duke of Fengyang County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ming—in the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei—inherited the title Duke of Fengyang County for Liang Chun's service.

sentences.zh: 尋授大都督，遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍，治小吏部，歷小御伯、御正下大夫。

translations.literal: Soon appointed grand area commander, transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-in-three-departments, and scattered cavalry regular attendant; directed the lesser department of personnel, passed through lesser chief of the imperial guard and assistant director under the imperial rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand area commander, then grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-in-three-departments, and scattered cavalry regular attendant; he directed the lesser department of personnel and served as lesser chief of the imperial guard and assistant director under the imperial rectifier.

sentences.zh: 保定五年，詔襲椿爵，舊封回授弟朗。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Baoding, an edict ordered him to inherit Chun's noble rank; the old enfeoffment was returned and granted to his younger brother Lang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Baoding an edict ordered him to inherit Liang Chun's title; the old enfeoffment was returned and given to his younger brother Lang.

sentences.zh: 天和中，改封樂陵郡公，除上州刺史，增邑幷前四千三百戶。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Leiling Commandery, removed [from current post] and made governor of Shang Province, fief together with previous four thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhe his title was changed to Duke of Leiling Commandery, he was made governor of Shang Province, and his combined fief rose to four thousand three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 梁臺字洛都，長池人也。

translations.literal: Liang Tai, styled Luodu, was a man of Changchi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tai, styled Luodu, came from Changchi.

sentences.zh: 父去斤，魏獻文時為隴西郡守。

translations.literal: His father Qujin in the time of Emperor Xianwen of Wei was administrator of Longxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qujin had served as administrator of Longxi commandery under Emperor Xianwen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 臺少果敢，有志操。

translations.literal: Tai from youth was bold and resolute, with lofty aspiration and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tai was bold and resolute from youth, with firm purpose and character.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，從爾朱天光討平關、隴，一歲之中，大小二十餘戰，以功授子都督，賜爵隴城鄉男。

translations.literal: During Xiaochang, following Erzhu Tianguang he suppressed and pacified Guan and Long; within one year, in big and small engagements more than twenty, for merit appointed sub-area commander and granted noble rank as Baron of Longcheng Township.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiaochang he followed Erzhu Tianguang in pacifying Guan and Long; within one year he fought more than twenty engagements large and small, was made sub-area commander, and enfeoffed Baron of Longcheng Township.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，進授都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai, advanced and appointed area commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai he was promoted to area commander.

sentences.zh: 後隸侯莫陳悅討南秦州羣盜，平之。

translations.literal: Later attached to Houmochen Yue in suppressing the bandits of South Qinzhou, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Houmochen Yue, he helped suppress the bandits of South Qinzhou and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 悅表臺為假節、衛將軍、左光祿大夫，進封隴城縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Yue memorialized Tai as provisional commissioner, general of the guard, left grand master of splendid wealth, advanced in enfeoffment to Baron of Longcheng County, fief two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Yue memorialized for Liang Tai to receive provisional credentials as general of the guard and left grand master of splendid wealth, and for his enfeoffment to be advanced to Baron of Longcheng County with two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋行天水郡事，轉行趙平郡事。

translations.literal: Soon acted as administrator of Tianshui commandery, transferred to act as administrator of Zhaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He soon acted as administrator of Tianshui commandery, then of Zhaoping commandery.

sentences.zh: 頻治郡，頗有聲績。

translations.literal: Repeatedly governing commanderies, he had considerable reputation and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Serving repeatedly as commandery administrator, he won a solid reputation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，天光追臺還，引入帳內。

translations.literal: Before long, Tianguang recalled Tai and brought him into the inner tent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Tianguang recalled Liang Tai and brought him into his inner tent.

sentences.zh: 及天光敗於寒陵，賀拔岳又引為心膂。

translations.literal: When Tianguang was defeated at Hanling, He Ba Yue again drew him close as trusted aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianguang was defeated at Hanling, He Ba Yue again drew Liang Tai close as a trusted aide.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所害，臺與諸將議翊戴太祖。

translations.literal: When Yue was murdered by Houmochen Yue, Tai with the various generals deliberated on supporting and enthroning the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: After Houmochen Yue murdered He Ba Yue, Liang Tai and the other generals deliberated on raising Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to command.

sentences.zh: 從討悅，破之。

translations.literal: Following in suppressing Yue, he defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the campaign against Houmochen Yue and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 又拜天水郡守。

translations.literal: Again appointed administrator of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed administrator of Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 大統初，復除趙平郡守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, again removed [from current post] and made administrator of Zhaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he was again made administrator of Zhaoping commandery.

sentences.zh: 又與太僕石猛破兩山屠各，詔增邑一百戶，轉平涼郡守。

translations.literal: Again with Grand Mentor Shi Meng broke the Two Mountains Tuge; an edict increased fief one hundred households, transferred to administrator of Pingliang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Grand Mentor Shi Meng in defeating the Two Mountains Tuge; an edict added one hundred households to his fief and transferred him to administrator of Pingliang commandery.

sentences.zh: 時莫折後熾結聚輕剽，寇掠居民。

translations.literal: At the time Moqi Houji gathered light raiders and plundered the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Moqi Houji gathered light raiders and plundered the people.

sentences.zh: 州刺史史寧討之，歷時不克。

translations.literal: The provincial governor Shi Ning suppressed him; over time could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governor Shi Ning attacked him but could not overcome him for a long while.

sentences.zh: 臺陳賊形勢，兼論攻取之策，寧善而從之，遂破賊徒。

translations.literal: Tai set forth the bandits' disposition and together discussed plans for attack and capture; Ning approved and followed, and thereupon broke the bandit forces.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tai analyzed the bandits' situation and laid out a plan of attack; Shi Ning approved and followed it, and they broke the bandits.

sentences.zh: 復與于謹破劉平伏。

translations.literal: Again with Yu Jin broke Liu Pingfu.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Yu Jin in defeating Liu Pingfu.

sentences.zh: 錄前後勳，授潁州刺史，賜姓賀蘭氏。

translations.literal: Recording achievements before and after, appointed governor of Ying Province and granted the surname Helan.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated service won him appointment as governor of Ying Province and the grant of the surname Helan.

sentences.zh: 從援玉壁，戰邙山，授帥都督。

translations.literal: Following in relief of Yubi, fighting at Mount Mang, appointed area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the relief of Yubi, fought at Mount Mang, and was made area commander.

sentences.zh: 大統十五年，拜南夏州刺史，加通直散騎常侍、本州大中正，增邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Datong, appointed governor of South Xia Province, added unembellished regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and chief rectifier of the province, fief increased two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Datong he was made governor of South Xia Province, given unembellished regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and chief rectifier of the province, and granted two hundred additional households.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，遷使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei, transferred to commissioner with credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-in-three-departments, advanced to grand general of fast cavalry and opening-office equal-in-three-departments, added palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was made commissioner with credentials, grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal-in-three-departments, then grand general of fast cavalry and opening-office equal-in-three-departments, with palace attendant added.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵中部縣公，增邑通前一千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, advanced in noble rank to Duke of Middle Commandery County, fief together with previous one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he was raised to Duke of Middle Commandery County with a combined fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武成中，從賀蘭祥征洮陽，先登有功，別封綏安縣侯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: During Wucheng, following Helan Xiang in campaigning against Taoyang, first to ascend with merit, separately enfeoffed Marquis of Suian County, fief one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: During Wucheng he followed Helan Xiang against Taoyang, was first over the wall, and was separately enfeoffed Marquis of Suian County with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 詔聽轉授其子元慶。

translations.literal: An edict permitted transferring it to his son Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted the title to be transferred to his son Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 保定四年，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, appointed grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Baoding he was made grand general.

sentences.zh: 時大軍圍洛陽，久而不拔。

translations.literal: At the time the great army besieged Luoyang and long could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the main army besieged Luoyang and could not take it for a long while.

sentences.zh: 齊騎奄至，齊公憲率兵禦之。

translations.literal: Qi cavalry suddenly arrived; Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian led troops to repulse them.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi cavalry suddenly arrived; Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian led troops to repulse them.

sentences.zh: 乃有數人為敵所執，已去陣二百餘步，臺望見之，憤怒，單馬突入，射殺兩人，敵皆披靡，執者遂得還。

translations.literal: Then several men were seized by the enemy, already more than two hundred paces from the formation; Tai saw it, was enraged, and alone on horseback charged in, shot and killed two men; the enemy all scattered, and the seized men were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Several men were then seized by the enemy more than two hundred paces from the line; Liang Tai saw it, flew into a rage, and charged in alone on horseback, shooting two men dead; the enemy scattered, and the captives got back safely.

sentences.zh: 齊公憲每歎曰：「梁臺果毅膽決，不可及也。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian often sighed and said: "Liang Tai is resolute and bold in decision—one cannot reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Qi Yuwen Xian often sighed and said: "Liang Tai is bold and resolute beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 」五年，拜鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year, appointed governor of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year Liang Tai was made governor of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 臺性疏通，恕己待物。

translations.literal: Tai by nature was open and penetrating, forgiving of himself and treating others generously.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Tai was open and easy by nature, strict with himself and generous toward others.

sentences.zh: 至於蒞民處政，尤以仁愛為心。

translations.literal: As to governing the people and handling administration, he especially took benevolence and love to heart.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people he above all kept benevolence at heart.

sentences.zh: 不過識千餘字，口占書啟，辭意可觀。

translations.literal: He knew scarcely more than a thousand characters; dictating letters and memorials, the wording and sense were presentable.
translations.idiomatic: He knew barely a thousand characters, yet dictating letters and memorials he produced respectable prose.

sentences.zh: 年過六十，猶能被甲跨馬，足不躡鐙。

translations.literal: Past sixty years old, he could still don armor and straddle a horse, his feet not touching the stirrups.
translations.idiomatic: Past sixty he could still don armor and mount a horse without touching the stirrups.

sentences.zh: 馳射弋獵，矢不虛發。

translations.literal: Galloping, shooting, and hunting—his arrows never missed.
translations.idiomatic: Galloping, shooting, and hunting, his arrows never missed.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang Tai died of illness.

sentences.zh: 宇文測字澄鏡，太祖之族子也。

translations.literal: Yuwen Ce, styled Chengjing, was a clansman of the Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce, styled Chengjing, was a kinsman of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 高祖中山、曾祖豆頹、祖騏驎、父永，仕魏，位並顯達。

translations.literal: High ancestor Zhongshan, great-grandfather Doutui, grandfather Qilin, and father Yong all served Wei and attained prominent rank.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears—Zhongshan, Doutui, Qilin, and his father Yong—had all served Northern Wei and risen to distinction.

sentences.zh: 測性沉密，少篤學，每旬月不窺戶牖。

translations.literal: Ce by nature was deep and secretive; from youth he devoted himself to study, for whole months and weeks not looking beyond door and window.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce was grave and reserved by nature; as a youth he studied intensely, sometimes going a month without leaving his study.

sentences.zh: 起家奉朝請、殿中侍御史，累遷司徒右長史、安東將軍。

translations.literal: He began his career as Attendant at Court and Palace Attendant Censor; through repeated promotion he became Right Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses and General Pacifying the East.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as attendant at court and palace attendant censor, then rose to right chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses and General Pacifying the East.

sentences.zh: 尚宣武女陽平公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Princess Yangping, daughter of Emperor Xuanwu, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Yangping, daughter of Emperor Xuanwu, and was made commandant of horse guards consort.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武疑齊神武有異圖，詔測詣太祖言，令密為之備。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei suspected Qi Shenwu of having other designs, he ordered Ce to go speak to the Grand Progenitor and secretly prepare against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu suspected Gao Huan of disloyal intent, he ordered Yuwen Ce to visit Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai and ask him to prepare in secret.

sentences.zh: 太祖見之甚歡。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor, seeing him, was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was delighted to receive him.

sentences.zh: 使還，封廣川縣伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: After sending him back, [Ce] was enfeoffed as Baron of Guangchuan county with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, Yuwen Ce was enfeoffed Baron of Guangchuan with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋從孝武西遷，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Xiaowu in the western migration and was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the emperor west and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 太祖為丞相，以測為右長史，軍國政事，多委任之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor became Chancellor, he made Ce Right Chief Clerk; military and state affairs were largely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai became chancellor, he made Yuwen Ce right chief clerk and entrusted him with much of military and civil administration.

sentences.zh: 又令測詳定宗室昭穆遠近，附於屬籍。

translations.literal: He also ordered Ce to assess in detail the clan's seniority and juniority, near and distant, and attach them to the register of kin.
translations.idiomatic: He also put Yuwen Ce in charge of sorting the imperial clan by seniority and distance and entering them in the genealogy.

sentences.zh: 除通直散騎常侍、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Appointed Supervising Cavalier Attendant and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising cavalier attendant and gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，拜侍中、長史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, appointed Palace Attendant and Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 4 (538) he was made palace attendant and chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 六年，坐事免。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because of an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督、行汾州事。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Bearer of the Staff, Fast Cavalry Grand General, Opening Office Equal to the Three Excellencies, Grand Commander, and acting inspector of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed bearer of the staff, fast cavalry grand general, opening-office equal-in-three-departments, grand commander, with acting charge of Fen Province.

sentences.zh: 測政存簡惠，頗得民和。

translations.literal: Ce's governance was spare and generous; he fairly won the people into harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce governed with simplicity and kindness and won the people to him.

sentences.zh: 地接東魏，數相鈔竊，或有獲其為寇者，多縛送之。

translations.literal: His territory bordered Eastern Wei; they frequently raided and stole from each other. When some were captured as bandits, many bound and sent them [to Ce].
translations.idiomatic: The province bordered Eastern Wei, where cross-border theft was frequent. Captured raiders were often bound and sent to Yuwen Ce.

sentences.zh: 測皆命解縛，置之賓館，然後引與相見，如客禮焉。

translations.literal: Ce always ordered the bonds loosed, had them placed in guest lodges, then led them out to meet, treating them with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce always had their bonds cut, lodged them as guests, and only then received them with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 仍設酒肴宴勞，放還其國，並給糧餼，衛送出境。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set out wine and food to feast and reward them, released them to their state, and moreover gave grain and provisions, escorting and sending them across the border.
translations.idiomatic: He then feasted them, sent them home with grain and provisions, and had them escorted safely across the border.

sentences.zh: 自是東魏人大慚，乃不為寇。

translations.literal: From this the people of Eastern Wei were greatly ashamed and no longer raided.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Eastern Wei people were ashamed and stopped raiding.

sentences.zh: 汾、晉之間，各安其業。

translations.literal: Between Fen and Jin, each settled to his trade.
translations.idiomatic: People on both sides of the Fen and Jin districts returned to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 兩界之民，遂通慶吊，不復為仇讐矣。

translations.literal: The people of both frontiers thereupon exchanged congratulations and condolences; they were no longer enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Border folk began to exchange congratulations and condolences and ceased to be enemies.

sentences.zh: 時論稱之，方于羊叔子。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time praised him, comparing him to Yang Shuozi.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion praised him and ranked him with Yang Hu.

sentences.zh: 或有告測與外境交通，懷貳心者。

translations.literal: There were those who reported that Ce had communication with the outer territory and harbored disloyal intent.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Yuwen Ce was dealing with the enemy and harbored disloyal intent.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒曰：「測為我安邊，吾知其無貳志，何為間我骨肉，生此貝錦！

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor in anger said: "Ce for me pacifies the frontier—I know he has no disloyal intent. Why drive a wedge between my kinfolk and raise this embroidered slander!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai raged: "Yuwen Ce holds my frontier—I know his heart is loyal. Who would drive a wedge between my own kin and weave this calumny!

sentences.zh: 」乃命斬之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the accuser beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " He had the accuser executed.

sentences.zh: 仍許測以便宜從事。

translations.literal: He still permitted Ce to act at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: He still allowed Yuwen Ce full discretion.

sentences.zh: 八年，加金紫光祿大夫，轉行綏州事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, added Golden Pigeon Grand Master of Splendor, transferred to acting inspector of Sui Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was given golden grand master of splendor and transferred to acting charge of Sui Province.

sentences.zh: 每歲河冰合後，突厥卽來寇掠，先是常預遣居民入城堡以避之。

translations.literal: Every year after the Yellow River ice joined, the Tujue at once came raiding and plundering. Formerly they always beforehand sent residents into castles to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Each year after the Yellow River froze, Turks came raiding. Before Yuwen Ce arrived, people were routinely evacuated into fortified towns.

sentences.zh: 測至，皆令安堵如舊。

translations.literal: When Ce arrived, he ordered all to dwell in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Ce arrived, he let everyone stay at home as usual.

sentences.zh: 乃於要路數百處並多積柴，仍遠斥候，知其動靜。

translations.literal: He then at several hundred points on key roads all piled much firewood, and also posted distant scouts to learn their movements.
translations.idiomatic: He stacked firewood at hundreds of key points along the roads and posted scouts far out to watch enemy movements.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，突厥從連穀入寇，去界數十裏。

translations.literal: That year in the twelfth month, Tujue entered raiding from Liangu, several tens of li from the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month that year the Turks invaded through Liangu, coming within several tens of li of the border.

sentences.zh: 測命積柴之處，一時縱火。

translations.literal: Ce ordered at the places where firewood was piled to fire all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce ordered all the firewood piles set ablaze at once.

sentences.zh: 突厥謂有大軍至，懼而遁走，自相蹂踐，委棄雜畜及輜重不可勝數。

translations.literal: The Tujue supposed a great army had arrived; in fear they fled, trampling each other, abandoning mixed livestock and baggage in numbers beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks thought a great army had arrived, fled in panic, trampled one another, and abandoned countless livestock and supplies.

sentences.zh: 測徐率所部收之，分給百姓。

translations.literal: Ce at ease led his command to gather it and distributed it to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce calmly collected the abandoned goods and distributed them among the people.

sentences.zh: 自是突厥不敢復至。

translations.literal: From this the Tujue did not dare come again.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Turks did not dare return.

sentences.zh: 測因請置戍兵以備之。

translations.literal: Ce thereupon requested that garrison troops be placed to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce then asked that garrison troops be posted as a permanent defense.

sentences.zh: 十年，徵拜太子少保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, summoned and appointed Junior Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recalled and made junior preceptor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，卒于位，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year, he died in office at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twelfth year he died in office at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太祖傷悼，親臨慟焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor grieved and mourned, coming in person to lament.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai mourned deeply and came in person to grieve.

sentences.zh: 仍令水池公護監護喪事。

translations.literal: He still ordered Duke of Chishui Hu to oversee funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He put Yuwen Hu, Duke of Chishui, in charge of the funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Given his former office posthumously; posthumous name Jing (Tranquil).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously confirmed in his rank; his posthumous name was Jing (Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 測性仁恕，好施與，衣食之外，家無蓄積。

translations.literal: Ce by nature was benevolent and forgiving, fond of giving; beyond food and clothing, the household had no accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce was benevolent and forgiving and generous by nature; apart from food and clothing his household kept no surplus.

sentences.zh: 在洛陽之日，曾被竊盜，所失物，卽其妻陽平公主之衣服也。

translations.literal: In the days at Luoyang, he once suffered theft; what was lost was none other than his wife Princess Yangping's clothing.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Luoyang he was once robbed of clothing belonging to his wife, Princess Yangping.

sentences.zh: 州縣擒盜，幷物俱獲。

translations.literal: The province and county seized the thief, and together with the goods all were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was caught and the stolen goods recovered.

sentences.zh: 測恐此盜坐之以死，乃不認焉。

translations.literal: Ce feared this thief would be punished with death for it, and so did not acknowledge [the goods as his].
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce feared the thief would be sentenced to death if the goods were identified, so he would not claim them.

sentences.zh: 遂遇赦得免。

translations.literal: Thereupon encountering an amnesty he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was spared when an amnesty came.

sentences.zh: 盜旣感恩，因請為測左右。

translations.literal: The thief, already grateful, thereupon requested to become Ce's attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful, the thief asked to serve as Yuwen Ce's attendant.

sentences.zh: 及測從魏孝武西遷，事極狼狽，此人亦從測入關，竟無異志。

translations.literal: When Ce followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the western migration, affairs were extremely chaotic; this man also followed Ce in entering the Passes, and in the end had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Ce followed Emperor Xiaowu's westward flight in chaos, this man followed him through the passes and stayed loyal to the end.

sentences.zh: 子該嗣。

translations.literal: His son Gai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 歷官內外，位至上開府儀同三司、臨淄縣公。

translations.literal: Through official posts internal and external, his rank reached Upper Opening Office Equal to the Three Excellencies and Duke of Linzi county.
translations.idiomatic: He served at court and in the provinces, rising to upper opening-office equal-in-three-departments and Duke of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 測弟深。

translations.literal: Ce's younger brother Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce's younger brother was Yuwen Shen.

sentences.zh: 深字奴干。

translations.literal: Shen, styled Nugan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen, styled Nugan.

sentences.zh: 性鯁正，有器局。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and straight, with capacity and scope.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and principled by nature, with breadth of vision.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，便累石為營伍，幷折草作旌旗，佈置行列，皆有軍陣之勢。

translations.literal: At only a few years, he piled stones as camps and barracks, and also broke grass to make banners and flags, deploying ranks and files—all with the momentum of army formations.
translations.idiomatic: As a small child he stacked stones into camps, fashioned grass into banners, and drew up ranks with the look of a real formation.

sentences.zh: 父永遇見之，乃大喜曰：「汝自然知此，於後必為名將。」

translations.literal: His father Yong happened to see it and thereupon greatly rejoiced, saying: "You naturally know this—later you will surely become a famous general."
translations.idiomatic: His father Yong saw it and said in delight: "You take to this by nature—you will be a famous general someday."

sentences.zh: 至永安初，起家秘書郎。

translations.literal: Reaching the beginning of Yongan, he began his career as Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongan era he entered service as secretary gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時羣盜蜂起，深屢言時事，爾朱榮雅知重之。

translations.literal: At the time bandits swarmed like bees; Shen repeatedly spoke on current affairs; Erzhu Rong by refinement knew and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry flared everywhere, Yuwen Shen spoke often on public affairs and Erzhu Rong came to value him.

sentences.zh: 拜厲武將軍。

translations.literal: Appointed Fearsome Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of fearsome martiality.

sentences.zh: 尋除車騎府主簿。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Chief Clerk of the Chariots and Cavalry Office.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became chief clerk of the chariots and cavalry office.

sentences.zh: 三年，授子都督，領宿衛兵卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, granted Son Commander, leading palace guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made commander of guards and put over the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武舉兵入洛，孝武西遷。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu raised troops and entered Luoyang, Xiaowu migrated west.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched on Luoyang and Emperor Xiaowu fled west,

sentences.zh: 旣事起倉卒，人多逃散，深撫循所部，並得入關。

translations.literal: Since the affair began in haste and many people fled and scattered, Shen soothed and guided those under his command, and all were able to enter the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: the crisis came suddenly and men scattered; Yuwen Shen kept his command together and brought them all through the passes.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵長樂縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit granted noble rank as Baron of Changle county.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Changle.

sentences.zh: 太祖以深有謀略，欲引致左右，圖議政事。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor because Shen had strategy and plan, wished to draw him close and consult on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, finding Yuwen Shen resourceful, wanted him near at hand to deliberate on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，乃啟為丞相府主簿，加朱衣直合。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he thereupon opened [the appointment] as Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Office, adding Red-Robe Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 1 (535) he was made chief clerk of the chancellor's office and given red-robed direct attendancy.

sentences.zh: 尋轉尚書直事郎中。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Direct-Affairs Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He soon moved on to direct-affairs gentleman in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武屯蒲阪，分遣其將竇泰趣潼關，高敖曹圍洛

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu encamped at Puban, he separately dispatched his general Dou Tai toward Tong Pass, and Gao Aocao besieged Luo
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan encamped at Puban he sent Dou Tai toward Tong Pass while Gao Aocao besieged Luo

translations.literal: (Yang)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yang]

translations.literal: [Prefecture].
translations.idiomatic: [emended: 州 → 陽].

sentences.zh: 太祖將襲泰，諸將咸難之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor was about to surprise Tai; the various generals all found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai planned a surprise attack on Dou Tai, but the generals all opposed it.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃隱其事，陽若未有謀者，而獨問策於深。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon concealed the matter, outwardly appearing as if without plan, while alone asking Shen's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai hid his plan, feigning indecision, and consulted Yuwen Shen alone.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「竇氏，歡之驍將也，頑凶而勇，戰亟勝而輕敵，歡每仗之，以為禦侮。

translations.literal: He replied: "The Dou clan are Huan's fierce generals—stubborn and fierce yet brave, in battle soon victorious yet slighting the enemy. Huan always relies on them as defense against insult.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Dou Tai is Gao Huan's fiercest general—brutal, brave, and quick to win, yet prone to underestimate the foe. Gao Huan trusts him as his shield.

sentences.zh: 今者大軍若就蒲阪，則高歡拒守，竇泰必援之，內外受敵，取敗之道也。

translations.literal: Now if the great army approaches Puban, then Gao Huan will hold defense and Dou Tai will surely aid him—attacked inside and outside, this is the way to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: If our main force moves on Puban, Gao Huan will stand on the defensive and Dou Tai will come to his aid—we would face enemies on two fronts and invite defeat.

sentences.zh: 不如選輕銳之卒，潛出小關。

translations.literal: Better to select light elite troops and secretly emerge at Xiao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Better to take elite light troops and slip out through Xiao Pass.

sentences.zh: 竇性躁急，必來決戰，高歡持重，未卽救之，則竇可擒也。

translations.literal: Dou by nature is rash and urgent; he will surely come to decisive battle. Gao Huan is deliberate; he will not immediately rescue—then Dou can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai is hot-tempered and will come out to fight. Gao Huan is cautious and will not rescue him at once—we can take Dou Tai.

sentences.zh: 旣虜竇氏，歡勢自沮。

translations.literal: Having captured the Dou clan, Huan's momentum will itself be dampened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dou Tai is taken, Gao Huan's spirit will break.

sentences.zh: 回師禦之，可以制勝。

translations.literal: Turning the army to resist him, one can achieve victory.
translations.idiomatic: Turn back and meet Gao Huan—you can win.

sentences.zh: 」太祖喜曰：「是吾心也。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor said with pleasure: "This is my heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said gladly: "That is exactly my thought.

sentences.zh: 」軍遂行，果獲泰而齊神武亦退。

translations.literal: " The army thereupon marched, and indeed captured Tai while Qi Shenwu also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " The army marched, Dou Tai was taken, and Gao Huan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 深又說太祖進取弘農，復克之。

translations.literal: Shen again persuaded the Grand Progenitor to advance and take Hongnong, again capturing it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen also urged an advance on Hongnong, which was taken again.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅，謂深曰：「君卽吾家之陳平也。」

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor greatly rejoiced and said to Shen: "You are my household's Chen Ping."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai was delighted and told Yuwen Shen: "You are our own Chen Ping."

sentences.zh: 是冬，齊神武又率大衆度河涉洛，至於沙苑。

translations.literal: That winter, Qi Shenwu again led a great host crossing the river and fording the Luo, reaching Shaya.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Gao Huan led a great army across the Yellow River and the Luo to Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆有懼色，唯深獨賀。

translations.literal: The generals all had fearful expressions; only Shen alone congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: The generals looked afraid; Yuwen Shen alone offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 太祖詰之，曰：「賊來充斥，何賀之有？

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor interrogated him, saying: "The bandits come in full force—what is there to congratulate?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai challenged him: "The enemy swarms upon us—what is there to celebrate?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「高歡之撫河北，甚得衆心，雖乏智謀，人皆用命，以此自守，未易可圖。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Gao Huan in pacifying Hebei has greatly won the people's hearts. Though lacking in wisdom and plan, the men all use their lives—in this he guards himself, not easy to scheme against.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered: "Gao Huan rules Hebei with great loyalty from his people. Though no great strategist, his men obey him absolutely—defending home ground he is hard to defeat.

sentences.zh: 今懸師度河，非衆所欲，唯歡恥失竇氏，愎諫而來。

translations.literal: Now an army suspended crossing the river is not what the multitude wishes; only Huan, shamed at losing the Dou clan, stubbornly rejected remonstrance and came.
translations.idiomatic: But he has crossed the river with his whole army against his men's wishes—Gao Huan comes only because he cannot bear the loss of Dou Tai and refused good counsel.

sentences.zh: 所謂忿兵，一戰可以擒也。

translations.literal: What is called an army of wrath—in one battle they can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: This is an army driven by rage; one battle will bring them down.

sentences.zh: 此事昭然可見，不賀何為。

translations.literal: This affair is plainly visible—if not congratulating, what would one do?
translations.idiomatic: That is plain enough—why would I not celebrate?

sentences.zh: 請假深一節，發王羆之兵，邀其走路，使無遺類矣。

translations.literal: I request to borrow Shen one tally of authority, to dispatch Wang Pi's troops, intercept their route of flight, and leave none surviving.
translations.idiomatic: Give me command of a detachment and Wang Pi's troops to cut off their retreat, and not one of them will escape.

sentences.zh: 」太祖然之。

translations.literal: " The Grand Progenitor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋而大破齊神武軍，如深所策。

translations.literal: Soon he greatly broke Qi Shenwu's army, as Shen had planned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Huan's army was routed, just as Yuwen Shen had foretold.

sentences.zh: 四年，從戰河橋。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he followed in battle at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he fought at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 六年，別監李弼軍討白額稽胡，並有戰功。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he separately supervised Li Bi's army in suppressing the White-Browed Ji Hu, both having battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he oversaw Li Bi's campaign against the White-Browed Qihu and won distinction in both.

sentences.zh: 俄進爵為侯，曆通直散騎常侍、東雍州別駕、使持節、大都督、東雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon advanced to marquis; served as Supervising Cavalier Attendant, Eastern Yongzhou Vice Governor, Bearer of the Staff, Grand Commander, and Governor of Eastern Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to marquis and served in succession as supervising cavalier attendant, vice governor of Eastern Yongzhou, bearer of the staff, grand commander, and governor of Eastern Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 深為政嚴明，示民以信，抑挫豪右，吏民懷之。

translations.literal: Shen in governing was strict and bright, showing the people faith, suppressing and checking the powerful and great; officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen governed with strict fairness, built trust with the people, and reined in the local power-holders, winning officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 十七年，入為雍州別駕。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, he entered [the capital] as Vice Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he entered court as vice governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, advanced to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal-in-three-departments, and cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜小吏部下大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, appointed Lesser Clerk of the Ministry of Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: When the six-office system was introduced, he was made lesser clerk of the Ministry of Clerks.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝受襌，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，遷吏部中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin received the abdication, [he] was advanced to Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Opening Office Equal in Three Departments, and transferred as Middle Grand Master of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, Yuwen Shen was raised to Grand General of Fast Cavalry and Opening Office Equal in Three Departments, and made middle grand master of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，除

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng, removed [from current post] and made Governor of
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng he was made governor of

translations.literal: (You)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: You]

sentences.zh: 〔豳〕州刺史，改封安化縣公。

translations.literal: [Bin] Province, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Anhua county.
translations.idiomatic: Bin Province, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Anhua.

sentences.zh: 二年，征拜宗師大夫，轉軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the second year, summoned and appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Clan, transferred as army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled as grand master of the imperial clan, then transferred as army marshal.

sentences.zh: 保定初，除京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, removed [from current post] and made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoding he was made metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 入為司會中大夫。

translations.literal: Entered court as Middle Grand Master of the Department of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as middle grand master director of accounts.

sentences.zh: 深少喪父，事兄甚謹。

translations.literal: Shen lost his father in youth and served his elder brother with great propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shen lost his father as a boy and served his elder brother Yuwen Ce with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 性多奇譎，好讀兵書。

translations.literal: By nature he had much unconventional cleverness and loved reading military books.
translations.idiomatic: Inventive and cunning by nature, he loved military treatises.

sentences.zh: 旣在近侍，每進籌策。

translations.literal: Once in close attendance, he often presented plans and stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the sovereign's side, he often offered strategic counsel.

sentences.zh: 及在選曹，頗獲時譽。

translations.literal: When in the Selection Bureau, he quite gained contemporary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Selection Bureau he won considerable contemporary esteem.

sentences.zh: 性仁愛，情隆宗黨。

translations.literal: By nature loving and kind, his affection for the clan flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Kind by nature, he cherished his clan deeply.

sentences.zh: 從弟神

translations.literal: His younger cousins Shen
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousins Shen

translations.literal: (Yu)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Yu]

sentences.zh: 〔舉〕、神慶幼孤，深撫訓之，義均同氣，世亦以此稱焉。

translations.literal: [Ju] and Shen Qing were orphaned young; Shen raised and instructed them, righteousness equal to sharing the same breath; the age also for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ju and Shen Qing were orphaned as boys; Yuwen Shen reared and taught them as if they were full brothers, and the age praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、少師、恆雲蔚三州刺史，諡曰成康。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff, Junior Preceptor, Governor of the three provinces Heng, Yun, and Wei; posthumous title Chengkang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made bearer of the staff, junior preceptor, and governor of Heng, Yun, and Wei provinces, with the posthumous title Chengkang.

sentences.zh: 子孝伯，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Xiaobo has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuwen Xiaobo has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太祖屬禍亂之辰，以征伐定海內，大則連兵百萬，系以存亡，小則轉戰邊亭，不闋旬月。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The Grand Progenitor belonged to an age of calamity and disorder; by campaigns and attacks he settled all within the seas—in great matters linking armies of a million on whom survival or extinction hung, in small matters turning battle at frontier posts without pause for ten-day periods.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai rose in an age of chaos and, through conquest, pacified the realm—great campaigns marshaled a million men with the fate of the state at stake, while lesser fights raged at border outposts month after month without letup.

sentences.zh: 是以人無少長，士無賢愚，莫不投筆要功，橫戈請奮。

translations.literal: Therefore whether person young or old, gentleman worthy or foolish, none failed to cast aside the pen to seek merit, level the spear and ask to strive.
translations.idiomatic: Young and old, worthy and simple alike cast aside the brush to win glory and grasped spear to volunteer for battle.

sentences.zh: 若夫數將者，並攀翼雲漢，底績屯夷，雖運移年世，而名成終始，美矣哉！

translations.literal: As for the several generals, all climbed wings to the clouded heavens, achieved merit in founding the age—though fortune shifted through years and generations, their names were completed from start to finish—how beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: These commanders all rose to wing the heavens, establishing merit in a time of upheaval; though years passed and fortunes turned, their fame endured from first to last—how splendid!

sentences.zh: 以赫連達之先識，而加之以仁恕；

translations.literal: Taking He Lianda's foresight, and adding to it kindness and forbearance;
translations.idiomatic: He Lianda had foresight, tempered with kindness and forbearance;

sentences.zh: 蔡祐之敢勇，而終之以不伐。

translations.literal: Cai You's daring courage, and ending with not boasting;
translations.idiomatic: Cai You had daring courage, yet never boasted of it.

sentences.zh: 斯豈企及所致乎，抑亦天性也。

translations.literal: Is this not what striving to reach brings about? Or rather also innate nature.
translations.idiomatic: Were these qualities achieved only by effort? In part—but also by native character.

sentences.zh: 宇文測昆季，政績謀猷，咸有可述，其當時之良臣歟。

translations.literal: Yuwen Ce and his brothers—in government achievement and strategic counsel all have what can be narrated—they are the good ministers of the age, are they not?
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Ce and his brothers left records of governance and strategy worth telling—they were among the finest ministers of their day.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
